digest:
**January 1950**
* **Jan. 11**: Student Council considers a resolution to hold an all-student vote on restrictive membership clauses and the Michigan plan.
* **Jan. 11**: Former missionary to Korea Dr. William E. Shaw receives an honorary Doctor of Divinity degree in chapel.
* **Jan. 18**: Renowned violinist Isaac Stern performs a program of Bach, Beethoven, and Stravinsky in Gray Chapel.
* **Jan. 18**: Student Council approves a proposal for an experimental campus honor system.
* **Jan. 18**: The basketball team breaks school scoring records in a 93-61 victory over Denison.

**February 1950**
* **Feb. 10**: The student body votes "no" on all ballot questions regarding the elimination of restrictive clauses in campus organizations.
* **Feb. 10**: Ruth Ann Firing is crowned 1950 Le Bijou Queen during a dance featuring Elliot Lawrence and his orchestra.
* **Feb. 22**: Student Council reverses its prior position and votes 15-1 against the Interfraternity Council plan.
* **Feb. 22**: Republican National Committee Chairman Guy G. Gabrielson and Democratic Vice-Chairman India Edwards speak on campus during political recruitment events.

**March 1950**
* **March 1**: Jud Millhon breaks the Edwards Gym scoring record with 54 points in a 95-81 basketball win against Ohio Northern.
* **March 15**: Students vote 956 to 44 to adopt the alternative voting system for campus elections, eliminating primaries.
* **March 22**: Jud Millhon is elected Student Body President in a five-candidate election under the new voting system.

**April 1950**
* **April 19**: Ken Gettelman and Paul Finical are appointed editors of *The Transcript* and *Le Bijou*, respectively.
* **April 19**: *The Transcript* wins first place and a $500 award in a national college newspaper safe-driving contest.
* **April 26**: University President Arthur S. Flemming criticizes congressional Red-hunting investigations as "decidedly unfair" during a chapel address.

**May 1950**
* **May 10**: Panhellenic Council adopts a new policy shifting sorority rushing to the period between first and second semesters starting in 1951.
* **May 10**: Herman M. Shipps is appointed Vice President of University Relations.
* **May 17**: The university announces a voluntary student health and accident insurance plan to take effect in the fall.

**September 1950**
* **Sept. 27**: Air Force ROTC enrollment increases sharply, jumping from 37 to 236 cadets.
* **Sept. 27**: The Bishop football team opens its 1950 season with a 60-14 victory over Otterbein.
* **Sept. 27**: Delta Gamma sorority moves into its newly purchased house at 148 W. Winter St.

**October 1950**
* **Oct. 4**: Lt. William H. (Bill) Shaw, 1943 student body president, is killed in action near Seoul, Korea.
* **Oct. 18**: The annual Campus Chest drive launches with a $10,000 fundraising goal.
* **Oct. 25**: Author Lillian Smith delivers a lecture titled "Whole Men in a Whole World" in Gray Chapel.
* **Oct. 25**: Virginia Figley is elected Homecoming Queen as the Bishops defeat previously undefeated Denison 33-13.

**November 1950**
* **Nov. 8**: The university community mourns the sudden death of long-time English professor Marie Drennan.
* **Nov. 8**: Socialist presidential candidate Norman Thomas visits campus to speak on peace and international affairs.
* **Nov. 8**: The football team upsets undefeated Mount Union 27-9 at Selby Stadium.
* **Nov. 15**: Masa Powers Nakayama is awarded an honorary Doctor of Laws degree by President Flemming.

**December 1950**
* **Dec. 6**: Broadway star Frances Starr performs alongside the Wesleyan Players in Sidney Howard's drama "The Silver Chord."
* **Dec. 6**: President Flemming is elected a national vice-president of the National Council of Churches of Christ in America.
* **Dec. 13**: Senior Bob Gardner is chosen as the 1950 "Safe Driving King" as faculty members assist with local street traffic monitoring.

**January**

* **Jan. 10:**
  * **Administration & Military Draft:** President Arthur S. Flemming addresses students on the Selective Service and draft situation, comparing it to the period following Pearl Harbor, while noting that plans for summer school remain undecided. Male students begin enlisting or leaving for the armed services amid draft threats, causing leadership changes in campus organizations such as radio honorary AER.
  * **Campus Development & Finances:** Drawings for the Pfeiffer Memorial natatorium by architect Rollin Rosser are set for bid submissions around March 1. The 1950 Alumni Fund drive finishes with $66,312 raised, and OWU professors become covered under Social Security benefits following a 1950 amendment.
  * **National & Global Leadership:** President Flemming is named head of a Columbus fund drive for Japan International University. Meanwhile, sociology professor Dr. Ira De A. Reid speaks on "Crises Clarity" at Convocation, and 1,300 college leaders from YMCA/YWCA groups gather at Miami University to discuss contemporary problems.
  * **Academics & Publications:** The chemistry department introduces Chemistry 201 for non-chemistry students. Senior Ellen McDougal is appointed editor of *OWL*, succeeding Ruth Ice. OWU hosts an invitational debate tournament in Gray Chapel featuring ten participating universities.
  * **Athletics:** The men's basketball team defeats Heidelberg 74-46, while the freshman "Baby Bishops" win their season opener against Heidelberg 72-40. The swim team defeats Lutheran 54-21, and the AFROTC rifle team prepares to compete in the 30th annual William Randolph Hearst ROTC rifle contest.
  * **Arts & Student Life:** Associated Women Students (AWS) hosts a tea at Monnett Hall for Lord and Lady Wakehurst of Great Britain during their U.S. tour. Guest performers for January include concert violinist Ruggiero Ricci and actress Eva Le Gallienne. Twelve sororities prepare for formal rushing at the end of examination week, while the freshman class hosts a "Bowery" themed party in the TUB.

**January 1952**

* **Jan. 9**: The Alumni Fund surpasses its $72,900 goal, raising $75,620 for faculty salaries under chairman John S. Pyke.
* **Jan. 9**: Dr. Arthur S. Flemming, chairman of the Manpower Policy Committee, highlights the national shortage of scientific, technical, and engineering personnel.
* **Jan. 9**: Eighteen students receive $500 in Robson prizes presented by Dr. Ernest F. Amy for outstanding term papers.
* **Jan. 9**: Korean student Okgill Kim prepares to leave campus to teach at Ewha Women's University, operating in exile in Pusan.
* **Jan. 9**: Republican presidential contender Harold E. Stassen asks to be released from a Jan. 18 chapel lecture until after the Ohio primaries.
* **Jan. 9**: Sen. John W. Bricker accepts an invitation from the Young Republicans to return to campus on Feb. 18 for Republican Recruitment Day.
* **Jan. 9**: French pianist Monique de la Bruchollerie presents the second Artists Series concert in Gray Chapel, performing works by Bach, Chopin, and Debussy.
* **Jan. 9**: Campus pledge classes combine forces to clear land behind Selby Stadium for a city park development project.
* **Jan. 9**: Installation of the cable in the Memorial Union elevator is completed, altering the building's organization.
* **Jan. 9**: The Wesleyan cagers defeat Heidelberg 76-66 after dropping three consecutive road games to Case, Akron, and Toledo during vacation.
* **Jan. 9**: Holiday Hill recreation place, destroyed by fire on Dec. 21, will be rebuilt by owner John Rowland as weather permits.
* **Jan. 9**: Pan-Hellenic Council votes to assess sorority members to provide $75 in financial aid to two women foreign students.

**January 1953**

* **Jan. 14**: **Administration & Campus Development** — University Treasurer D. J. Hornberger announced that Ohio Wesleyan received over $325,000 in scholarship endowments during the second half of 1952. The Ford Foundation awarded $20,000 to support the university's two-year curriculum study. Trustees officially renamed the Institute of Practical Politics after its founder, Dr. Ben A. Arneson. Additionally, Placement Bureau Director Mrs. Donald Boecklin announced the permanent abolition of the $2 senior placement fee.
* **Jan. 14**: **Campus News & National Events** — Heavy fog grounded General George C. Marshall's plane in Washington, forcing the cancellation of his scheduled campus lecture. OWU hosted a regional National Student Association (NSA) conference at the Memorial Union building for Ohio and Indiana colleges, featuring NSA travel assistant director Mary O'Dea speaking on European tours. The YWCA launched an all-campus drive collecting hundreds of pounds of clothing for Korean relief. Sophomore Patricia Kelley was selected as Delaware County Sesquicentennial queen.
* **Jan. 14**: **Academics & Debates** — Ohio State University and Muskingum College took top honors at OWU's Annual Invitational Debate Tournament. Meanwhile, varsity debaters George Ross, Ken Creasy, and Steve Crites represented OWU at the Oberlin Student Congress, and a split-team debate with Denison University was arranged for Chapel.
* **Jan. 14**: **Arts & Entertainment** — The freshman play, Samuel Taylor's comedy *"The Happy Time"* directed by Ada Humpreville, opened for an arena showing. The Social Committee announced that Ralph Marterie and his orchestra will play the second semester Registration Dance on Feb. 3. Duo-pianists Vera Appleton and Michael Field appeared in Gray Chapel, while the University Concert Band under Charles Thompson delivered its second recital. 
* **Jan. 14**: **Athletics** — Men's basketball picked up Ohio Conference victories against Heidelberg (92-85) and Denison (81-74) alongside a tight overtime loss to Wittenberg (96-92), led in scoring by guard Bob Kimble. The swim team suffered its first loss of the season, falling 43-41 to Kent State after dropping the final freestyle relay.

**January 1954**

* **Jan. 13:** Mrs. Franklin D. Roosevelt is scheduled to speak at Gray Chapel as part of the Lecture-Movie series.
* **Jan. 13:** Construction contracts for new Phi Gamma Delta and Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity houses are set to be awarded.
* **Jan. 13:** The university opened its new Pfeiffer Memorial Natatorium, marked by an upcoming open house and swim meets against Ohio University, Central State, and Albion.
* **Jan. 13:** Case Institute of Technology announced the cancellation of its 1954 football season due to lack of student interest and rising costs, resulting in OWU losing a scheduled game.
* **Jan. 13:** The Ohio Wesleyan Alumni Fund surpassed its $93,000 goal, bringing in $96,016.12.
* **Jan. 13:** Alumnus Ralph E. Halls donated nearly $12,000 to the university to establish an award for selected chemistry majors.
* **Jan. 13:** Four science students—Robert Cotner, Leonard Treash, George Arnold, and Thomas Mead—were awarded $400 Armco scholarships.
* **Jan. 13:** The faculty approved curriculum expansions across multiple departments, including new courses in Russian history, sculpture, magazine article writing, an expanded two-semester astronomy sequence, and two credit hours for Air Force ROTC summer camp.
* **Jan. 13:** Ray Anthony and his orchestra were booked to perform at the campus registration dance on Feb. 2.
* **Jan. 13:** Six OWU debaters went undefeated at the Otterbein College Invitational Debate Tournament, placing first among 15 competing colleges.
* **Jan. 13:** The student observatory announced special open hours to allow students and faculty to view a total eclipse of the moon.
* **Jan. 13:** The OWU sailing team achieved a first-place ranking in the Mid-West Sailing Conference with a .797 winning percentage.
* **Jan. 13:** The men's basketball team snapped a five-game losing streak by defeating Heidelberg 86-58, following a challenging Christmas trip to New York and a narrow 69-66 conference loss to Wittenberg.

**January 1955**
* **Jan. 12:** Concert pianist Gina Bachauer performs in Chapel as part of the University Artist Series.
* **Jan. 12:** Sen. J. William Fulbright delivers a speech in Gray Chapel on "The United States in World Affairs."
* **Jan. 12:** The Speech Department sponsors an Ohio invitational debate tournament featuring approximately 12 universities.
* **Jan. 12:** Socialist leader Norman Thomas is announced as the headline speaker for the upcoming Religious Emphasis-International Affairs Week.
* **Jan. 12:** Historian and Columbia University professor Henry Steele Commager is scheduled to speak at Chapel.
* **Jan. 12:** Campus Chest exceeds its $4,000 goal by collecting $4,150; the 1954 Alumni Fund reports raising $104,998, surpassing its goal by nearly $5,000.
* **Jan. 12:** Student Council survey results reveal a 3-to-1 preference among students for a full weekend Thanksgiving vacation.
* **Jan. 12:** Phi Gamma Delta begins moving into its newly completed Wilkinson Lodge.
* **Jan. 12:** A national AFROTC liaison officer arrives on campus to inspect the administration and training methods of Ohio Wesleyan's ROTC unit.
* **Jan. 12:** Seven political science majors plan a tour of Washington, D.C. (Jan. 26–28) to observe federal government operations.
* **Jan. 12:** In athletics, the wrestling team drops its season opener 33-0 to Bowling Green, while the basketball team splits games with Hiram (81-79 win) and Denison (82-79 loss).

**May 1955**
* **May 25:** The Interfraternity Council unanimously passes legislation establishing fines of $10 to $200 for fraternities participating in riots or unauthorized demonstrations.
* **May 25:** Athletic Director George Gauthier is honored at a surprise Chapel upon his retirement after 34 years at OWU; Coach Robert Strimer is tipped to succeed him.
* **May 25:** Charles Malik and Norman Vincent Peale are announced as commencement and baccalaureate speakers for the 111th graduation exercises.
* **May 25:** Assistant Dean of Women Olive P. McCarty resigns to accept the post of Dean of Women at Youngstown College.
* **May 25:** Association of Women Students (AWS) defeats a proposed plan for automatic 12 o'clock curfews during final examination week.
* **May 25:** Monnett Hall bathroom renovation plans are postponed for the summer due to high construction bids exceeding available funds, while Library Director J. Herrold Lancaster calls for urgent expansion of overcrowded Slocum Library.
* **May 25:** In sports, the Bishop golf team edges Denison at Granville to win the Ohio Conference Championship, Shirl Turvey wins her second consecutive Ohio Women's Intercollegiate Tennis title, and the men's tennis team finishes second in the conference.
* **May 25:** The campus ROTC drill team wins the first annual competition held on Edwards Field among local detachment colleges.
* **May 25:** Internationally, four occupation powers sign the Austrian State Treaty at Belvedere Palace on May 15, restoring independence to Austria.

**January 1956**
* **Jan. 11**: Interim-President Frank J. Prout announces that the fate of three AFROTC sub-units will be determined within two weeks, while Air Force officials rule out a planned AFROTC Drill Team trip to the Mardi Gras.
* **Jan. 11**: Draft of the new Student Government Constitution experiences delays due to disagreements over representation.
* **Jan. 11**: Interim-President Prout appeals to the Ford Foundation for a supplementary "accomplishment grant" similar to those awarded to Oberlin, Denison, DePauw, and Wooster.
* **Jan. 11**: Arthur S. Flemming, president-on-leave and defense mobilization director, reiterates that he is not interested in the presidency at Ohio State University.
* **Jan. 11**: Slocum Library receives a $1,000 grant to support its cooperative project with Denison and Kenyon libraries.
* **Jan. 11**: The university receives a $27,700 bequest from the late Isaac N. Reitenour, an Indiana businessman who never attended college.
* **Jan. 11**: The Alumni Fund exceeds its 1955 goal, collecting $107,146.28 from approximately 5,000 donors.
* **Jan. 11**: Prof. J. Allen Hynek is named to select global observation sites for projected man-made satellites, and scientists prepare to use Perkins Observatory's 69-inch telescope to analyze gases on Mars.
* **Jan. 11**: A Christmas morning fire heavily damages the Midway Restaurant, leaving its reopening date uncertain.
* **Jan. 11**: Delaware citizens assure funding for a new recreation area by surpassing the drive goal for Blue Limestone Lake Park.
* **Jan. 11**: The OWU Ice Hockey Club defeats Denison 5-4 at the Marion Coliseum, while the varsity swim team opens its season with a 52-32 win over Wittenberg.
* **Jan. 11**: The basketball team drops an 82-85 Ohio Conference game to Denison despite 27 points from Jim Hibbitts, following an earlier 67-62 victory over an Alumni squad in OWU's first Olympic Fund benefit game.
* **Jan. 11**: Five OWU soccer players earn All-Midwest Soccer Squad honors.

**January**
* **Jan. 9**: The National Science Foundation grants Ohio Wesleyan $57,300 to conduct an eight-week summer institute for high school science teachers.
* **Jan. 9**: Two professors, Loyd D. Easton (Philosophy Department chairman) and Donald C. Eyssen (associate professor of speech), are granted second-semester leaves of absence.
* **Jan. 9**: Phi Kappa Tau is expected to vote to end delayed fraternity pledging on campus.
* **Jan. 9**: A local service club committee makes plans to host four Hungarian refugee students expected to enroll in the fall.
* **Jan. 9**: Ohio Wesleyan receives a 240-acre farm near Tuscola, Ill., valued at $140,000, willed by alumna Clara Olney Reeves.
* **Jan. 9**: A business magazine article notes that President-on-leave Arthur S. Flemming's work in Washington warrants continued service, despite his plans to return to OWU soon.
* **Jan. 9**: The Ohio Wesleyan Sailing Club places second in the Sugar Bowl Invitational Regatta in New Orleans, defeating 22 teams and last year's national champions.
* **Jan. 9**: The wrestling team opens its first season as a varsity sport against Wittenberg in Edwards Gym.
* **Jan. 9**: OWU football tackle and 1956 captain Ray Van Orden is named to an All-American team of Methodist-related colleges.

**January 1958**

* **Jan. 15**: Junior Tom Schooley broke the U.S. Senate filibuster record by 27 minutes during a "talkathon," holding the floor for 24 hours and 45 minutes.
* **Jan. 15**: A proposal for OWU membership in the National Student Association (NSA) was defeated 26-3, ending membership efforts.
* **Jan. 15**: Acting Vice President and Dean George W. Burns announced an expected salary increase for OWU faculty members for the 1958-59 year.
* **Jan. 15**: President Arthur S. Flemming reported that classes will begin second semester in the new $900,000 Kathryn Sisson Phillips Hall.
* **Jan. 15**: The Board of Trustees executive committee prepared to decide on the proposed relocation of Perkins Observatory's 69-inch reflecting telescope to the Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona.
* **Jan. 15**: A national chapter of Sigma Xi, a professional science honorary society, was officially installed at Ohio Wesleyan.
* **Jan. 15**: The 1957 Alumni Fund exceeded its $150,000 goal by $4,725.85, according to Fund Director Mrs. Glee Murray.
* **Jan. 15**: The Senior Show production of "Carousel" prepared to open a three-night run at the Willis High auditorium.
* **Jan. 15**: Actor Basil Rathbone was slated to narrate the OWU production of the oratorio "King David" during Monnett Week End.
* **Jan. 15**: Author and editor Eugene Exman was scheduled to speak at Gray Chapel regarding his book "The World of Albert Schweitzer."
* **Jan. 15**: Special student K. C. Yuen of Singapore stated during a simulated press conference that the Little Rock incident severely damaged U.S. prestige in the Far East.
* **Jan. 15**: Student Council received a report detailing the refusal of freshman women to accept the proposed SG Freshman Board.
* **Jan. 15**: Two OWU students were held in city jail awaiting charges after being picked up by police on West William Street.
* **Jan. 15**: Plans were announced for a European tour for the OWU Women's Glee Club and female members of the A Cappella choir.
* **Jan. 15**: Men's varsity basketball suffered a 73-72 loss to Denison, while the JV basketball team maintained an undefeated 7-0 record with a 76-68 victory over Denison.
* **Jan. 15**: OWU wrestling opened its season with an 18-14 win over Cincinnati, led by Bill Baysinger, who earned Athlete-of-the-Week honors.
* **Jan. 15**: The swimming team lost its first dual meet of the season to Oberlin, 48-38.
* **Jan. 15**: Ohio Governor C. William O'Neill delivered an address during Chapel.

**January 1959**

* **Jan. 14**: Dr. David A. Lockmiller, newly named 10th president of Ohio Wesleyan, will assume a part-time administrative role starting Feb. 1 while his former institution, the University of Chattanooga, seeks a successor. Lockmiller also presented six books to Slocum Library.
* **Jan. 14**: Institute of Practical Politics Director Fred G. Burke is named to the Delaware City Council, while sociology professor Russell Bayliff is appointed council representative to the Jane M. Case Hospital Board.
* **Jan. 14**: Former state atomic energy coordinator William H. Eells is expected to announce whether he will return to OWU's Political Science Department.
* **Jan. 14**: Harry S. Truman and Richard Nixon decline invitations to speak at Ohio Wesleyan during the second semester due to prior obligations.
* **Jan. 14**: Slocum Library opens the complete fourth deck of its stacks to students and receives a $200 gift from the Gluck Philosophy Foundation for permanent acquisitions. Meanwhile, Student Forum proposes measures to curb book thefts from open stacks.
* **Jan. 14**: The Interfraternity Council amends its by-laws to establish a deferred rushing program for the second semester, and the Panhellenic Council approves all-night sorority retreats in sorority houses.
* **Jan. 14**: Men's Court fines Sigma Phi Epsilon $300 and Phi Delta Theta $100 after both fraternity houses were found guilty of stealing Christmas trees in December.
* **Jan. 14**: Two 18-year-old local youths begin their second week of a 60-day jail sentence and face $800 in fines following unprovoked attacks on three OWU students.
* **Jan. 14**: Student Council creates a temporary committee to review and recommend revisions to campus automobile policy, with 254 driving permits issued to date.
* **Jan. 14**: Student Government's Academic Affairs Committee plans an evaluation booklet covering 60–70 selected courses, using input from honor students across 25 departments.
* **Jan. 14**: OWU announces plans to host a Model UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) conference Feb. 6–7, expecting 80 delegates from 18 Ohio colleges.
* **Jan. 14**: Vocalist Jane Morgan is booked to headline the Feb. 7 Registration Dance in Edwards Gym, where the 1959 *Le Bijou* queen will be crowned. French pianist Philippe Entremont presents an Artist Series concert in Gray Chapel, and Japanese woodcut artist Kiyoshi Saito's work goes on display in the MUB.
* **Jan. 14**: In athletics, basketball co-captain Dick Faul ranks second in Ohio Conference scoring, helping OWU defeat Kenyon 72-56, though the Bishops drop contests to Case Tech (58-57), Wittenberg (92-72), and St. Bonaventure (91-43).
* **Jan. 14**: Football end Dick DeHaven is named to the UPI All-Ohio team, the wrestling team defeats Cincinnati 21-8, and indoor track practice opens under Coach Sterling Geesman.

**January 1960**
- **Jan 13:** Men's Court convicts two sophomores of conduct unbecoming an OWU student for placing fraudulent long-distance phone calls.
- **Jan 13:** Student Body President Bryce Collier announces OWU's invitation to send a student delegate to the White House Conference on Children and Youth.
- **Jan 13:** The Administration decides to discontinue the Middle Eastern studies program next year due to budgetary considerations.
- **Jan 13:** Officials announce the 69-inch reflecting telescope at Perkins Observatory will relocate to Flagstaff, Arizona, for better weather conditions.
- **Jan 13:** Kappa Alpha Theta sorority announces plans to build a new chapter house beginning March 1.
- **Jan 13:** The Bishop cagers defeat Otterbein (93-67) and Denison, while the swim team overwhelms Muskingum (70-24).

**February 1960**
- **Feb 24:** Juniors George Conrades, Bob Maxwell, and Frank Ollendorff enter a three-way contest for Student Body President.
- **Feb 24:** Louis "Satchmo" Armstrong and his All-Stars perform before a packed crowd of over 1,600 in Gray Chapel.
- **Feb 24:** OWU hosts delegates from Oberlin and Antioch for the Five-College Conference winter weekend.
- **Feb 24:** Student Council approves a plan to install 12 additional telephones in women's residence halls.
- **Feb 24:** Joseph A. Neville, founder and promoter of the Little Brown Jug harness races, dies at his Delaware home.
- **Feb 24:** The OWU swim team extends its winning streak to 10 dual meets after defeating Baldwin Wallace (57-37) and Oberlin (65-30).

**March 1960**
- **Mar 16:** Sophomores Ray Esch and Paul Hart are named editors of the *Transcript* and *Le Bijou*, respectively.
- **Mar 16:** Student Body President George Conrades and Vice-President Alice McAllister officially assume office on Student Council.
- **Mar 16:** Alpha Sigma Phi wins the Greek Week fraternity song fest for the second consecutive year, and vocal group The Brothers Four headlines the Greek Week Ball.
- **Mar 16:** The OWU debate team takes second place out of 15 teams at the Northeast Ohio Conference Debate Tournament in Akron.
- **Mar 16:** OWU trackmen take third place in the Ohio Conference Indoor Track Championship, while Sigma Chi claims the intramural basketball title.

**April 1960**
- **April 13:** Arthur S. Flemming, Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare and former OWU president, delivers the Chapel address opening Republican Day.
- **April 13:** Student Council unanimously establishes a temporary Academic Directions Committee to give students input in university administration.
- **April 13:** Junior Bob Maxwell is appointed Chief Justice of Men's Court.
- **April 13:** Dr. H. Richard Niebuhr of Yale Divinity School delivers four Merrick Lectures focusing on Christian ethics.
- **April 13:** The varsity baseball team wins its home opener against Kenyon, 10-7.

**May 1960**
- **May 4:** Student group "Concern" launches a $2,000 fundraising drive, and the Board of Trustees approves tuition grants to assist Southern sit-in protesters expelled from their colleges.
- **May 4:** Expelled Alabama State student and sit-in leader Bernard Lee visits campus to share his experiences in Southern civil rights demonstrations.
- **May 4:** *The Transcript* earns All-American rating honors and state awards at the Ohio College Newspaper Association convention.
- **May 4:** Monnett Week End features a convocation address by Dr. Lillian Gilbreth, the Senior Show, and Dolphin Club synchronized swimming performances.
- **May 4:** The OWU baseball team defeats Denison 9-5 before preparing for its Monnett Day game against Otterbein.

**November 1960**
- **Nov 9:** Vice-President and Dean of the University George W. Burns announces his resignation at a faculty meeting.
- **Nov 9:** The Board of Trustees approves plans to break ground by June for an $805,000 science center building.
- **Nov 9:** The University institutes mandatory senior comprehensive examinations for graduation, effective with the junior class of 1962.
- **Nov 9:** Space travel authority Willy Ley lectures on "The Conquest of Space" in Gray Chapel.
- **Nov 9:** The football team defeats Wooster 11-3, knocking the Scots out of title contention before clashing with Wittenberg for the traditional Skull trophy.

**January 1961**

* **Jan. 11:** Ohio Wesleyan prepares to open its new University-owned bookstore on Feb. 1 in the remodeled former AFROTC building, while the non-profit student bookstore continues operating out of Quonset Hut No. 2.
* **Jan. 11:** President David A. Lockmiller takes the oath for the Ohio Bar in Columbus before Supreme Court Chief Justice Carl V. Weygandt and travels to Denver to preside over the Association of American Colleges meeting.
* **Jan. 11:** Student Council considers a one-day spring holiday proposal and hears a Student Forum request to extend Slocum Library hours to Sunday evenings.
* **Jan. 11:** Campus debates center on a proposed academic honor system, fraternity discrimination clauses, and low student turnout in recent campus referendums.
* **Jan. 11:** Congressman John Brademas (D-Ind.), former executive assistant to Adlai E. Stevenson, is scheduled to speak in chapel on "The Christian Faith and Political Action."
* **Jan. 11:** "Finian's Rainbow" is selected as the 1961 Senior Play, and the A Cappella Choir presents its Vesper Concert in Gray Chapel alongside the OWU Symphony.
* **Jan. 11:** In sports, the men's basketball team defeats Denison 72-55 to secure its ninth victory of the season, center Max Urick earns Little All-American honors, and the undefeated swimming team prepares to host Miami University, led by Olympic champion Bill Mulliken.

**April 1961**

* **Jan. 26 / Apr. 26:** The faculty issues a official condemnation of President David A. Lockmiller, escalating a campus leadership feud; Student Body President Lane McGaughy presents petitions with 875 student signatures supporting Student Council's call for a new president or an independent provost.
* **Apr. 26:** Registrar Allan C. Ingraham discloses that 138 students have requested transcripts amid the administration controversy, while Student Council hosts an open forum to address student concerns.
* **Apr. 26:** Ohio Wesleyan officially joins 11 other liberal arts institutions to form the Great Lakes College Association (GLCA).
* **Apr. 26:** A new mandatory mid-morning chapel-assembly policy allowing one cut per week is announced for the upcoming fall semester.
* **Apr. 26:** Alpha Chi Omega wins the Greek Week sorority song fest, breaking Delta Gamma's two-year winning streak, as Greek Week activities conclude across campus.
* **Apr. 26:** Women students vote in corridor meetings to reinstate the previous year's late minute policy.
* **Apr. 26:** In athletics, Commodore Ken Engler leads the OWU sailing club to victory at the Ohio Intercollegiate Sailing Championships, the baseball team routs Otterbein 16-3 behind Toby Aaron's four-hitter, and Selby Field hosts the 30th and final Ohio Wesleyan Relays.

**February 1962**
* **Feb. 14**: The Board of Trustees approves a $100 tuition increase for the fall semester alongside 11 faculty promotions.
* **Feb. 14**: Donald J. Hornberger announces his retirement as OWU vice-president and treasurer effective Sept. 1 after 41 years of service; University Controller Robert W. Meyer is named his successor.
* **Feb. 14**: Student Government places a proposed constitutional revision plan on the upcoming Mar. 19 ballot, while the SG Bookstore faces a final council verdict.
* **Feb. 14**: Former OWU President Arthur S. Flemming urges faculty leadership toward academic excellence, as the Presidential Selection Committee accelerates its search for a new university leader.
* **Feb. 14**: Campus Chest opens its 1962 fund drive with a $2,000 goal, and Alpha Sig entry Terry Dougherty wins the "Ugly Man" contest.
* **Feb. 14**: The men's basketball team reaches a 13-1 conference record, holding 21st place in the national UPI small college poll, with freshman Barry Clemens and swimmer Jim Brown named Athletes of the Week.
* **Feb. 14**: Senior offensive end Don Gerosa is awarded the Mike Gregory Memorial Award as the Outstanding Lineman in the Ohio Conference.
* **Feb. 14**: Acclaimed jazz pianist Ahmad Jamal is scheduled to perform at Gray Chapel following the OWU-Baldwin-Wallace basketball game.

**October 1962**
* **Oct. 31**: Author Aldous Huxley addresses the campus in Gray Chapel on the heels of the OWU Genetics Symposium, delivering a lecture on modern human choices.
* **Oct. 31**: Former OWU President Bishop Herbert Welch marks his 100th birthday after delivering the inaugural charge to newly installed President Elden T. Smith.
* **Oct. 31**: Student Government circulates petitions to open Slocum Library on Sunday nights, while a Senate committee works to extend women's visitation hours in fraternity houses.
* **Oct. 31**: The Limeliters perform at Gray Chapel, while upcoming assemblies schedule appearances by folk singer Tony Saletan and pacifist Albert Bigelow.
* **Oct. 31**: Coach Marv Frye's cross country team achieves a 7-1 season record after defeating Denison 15-50, and the women's field hockey team remains undefeated entering the Buckeye Tournament.
* **Oct. 31**: The Bishop football team falls 37-6 to Wittenberg in Springfield, preparing next to face Wabash College's single-wing offense.
* **Oct. 31**: Student Health Service Director Dr. F. W. Logan offers free flu shots to students to prevent an impending epidemic, and Circle K organizes student support for the Delaware United Appeals Drive.

**January 1963**

* **Jan. 16**: Faculty and Board vote on a proposed three-term curriculum while Student Council endorses the Academic Policy Committee's plan.
* **Jan. 16**: Ohio Wesleyan purchases the 12-acre Delaware Community Field, including stadium and courts, for $75,000 at a Board of Education auction.
* **Jan. 16**: Chief Justice Quinn Mills notes Men's Court may now have the authority to rule Student Government laws and actions unconstitutional.
* **Jan. 16**: President Elden T. Smith announces a $4,000 DuPont Company grant for science teaching and aims to name a new academic vice president by March 1.
* **Jan. 16**: Following a petition campaign, the library initiates Sunday night opening hours, attracting approximately 140 students on its first evening.
* **Jan. 16**: Students observe pigeons dying on campus after the city puts out poisoned corn to handle a bird population explosion.
* **Jan. 16**: Student Government reforms the Ugly Man Contest by outlawing the use of animal entrails and slaughterhouse scraps.
* **Jan. 16**: The Chapel Committee recommends reducing required chapel-assemblies from three to two per week; term fines for absences pass $1,800.
* **Jan. 16**: The Admissions Office reports receiving 1,114 applications for the incoming Class of 1967 as of Jan. 4.
* **Jan. 16**: Hans Schmidt-Isserstedt conducts the NDR Symphony Orchestra of Hamburg, Germany, in the third Artist Series performance.
* **Jan. 16**: Bishop cagers drop a 56-38 decision to Wittenberg, while the wrestling team defeats Kenyon.

**May 1963**

* **May 1**: Board of Trustees Chairman Phillip C. Ebeling dies at age 58 in Dayton's Miami Valley Hospital.
* **May 1**: *The Transcript* earns its sixth All-American rating in seven semesters along with three "Best in Ohio" honors.
* **May 1**: Seventeen Russian visitors arrive on campus for events and discussions; a rumored picket by student "minutemen" fails to materialize.
* **May 1**: Political speakers Carl Winter (Communist Party member) and Fulton "Buddy" Lewis III (ultra-conservative) are scheduled for Gray Chapel addresses.
* **May 1**: Men's leadership honorary Omicron Delta Kappa taps five students and basketball coach Frank Shannon.
* **May 1**: Student Senate ratifies Jerry Getz as Men's Court Chief Justice following a two-day debate and an emergency session.
* **May 1**: Spring Fever Day celebrations begin with the tradition of ringing the Stuyvesant Hall bell.
* **May 1**: The annual Campus Chest drive closes after raising $600, missing its $2,000 target.
* **May 1**: Religion instructor and YWCA director Miriam Willey resigns, marking the 14th faculty resignation announced.
* **May 1**: The NSF awards OWU's Chemistry Department a $20,000 grant to host a summer conference for college teachers in August.
* **May 1**: In athletics, lacrosse beats Kenyon 8-6, track takes second place at the Ohio Conference Relays behind Akron, and the sailing team wins the Area B Eliminations.

**January 1964**

* **Jan. 15**: Five Williams Drive fraternities face Men's Court charges after a vacation check reveals drinking violations and deplorable living conditions.
* **Jan. 15**: Final grades indicate that OWU's first term under the new 4-3-3 academic calendar is at least as successful as the previous semester system.
* **Jan. 15**: CBS television show *College Bowl* invites Ohio Wesleyan to select and field a team for a March 22 broadcast match.
* **Jan. 15**: Congressman John Ashbrook (R-Ohio) and Fulton Lewis III visit campus to analyze 1964 national election issues.
* **Jan. 15**: Author William L. Shirer speaks in Gray Chapel on "The United States In World Affairs."
* **Jan. 15**: SCORR joins the Delaware Civil Rights Committee to protest the local Elks Charity Minstrel show at Willis Auditorium.
* **Jan. 15**: A major gas main leak between freshman men's dormitories cuts off heat to the Williams Drive area for several hours.
* **Jan. 15**: Wooster hands the basketball team its first Ohio Conference loss (64-61), while the swim team defeats Wooster 52-42 and the matmen beat Baldwin-Wallace and Wooster.

**February 1964**

* **Feb. 19**: OWU Board of Trustees passes a policy statement on discrimination, freeing the administration to address individual campus bias cases.
* **Feb. 19**: Final architectural plans are unveiled for a new $1.5 million library, as debate continues over closing Franklin Street for campus expansion.
* **Feb. 19**: Eight student contestants begin daily drills competing for final positions on OWU's upcoming televised *College Bowl* squad.
* **Feb. 19**: Fraternities initiate 177 freshmen this winter, marking the largest initiation class since 1901.
* **Feb. 19**: Delaware Fire Department responds to two bogus alarms on campus, including calls at Monnett Hall and a fraternity row privy.
* **Feb. 19**: AWS submits its newly approved constitution to the faculty for final approval.
* **Feb. 19**: Scottish folk artist Jean Redpath performs in assembly, while Orchesis modern dance group prepares for its Gray Chapel recital.
* **Feb. 19**: The basketball team earns conference wins over Capital (73-58) and Kenyon, while wrestling edges Kenyon 20-14 with pins from heavyweight Bill Baird.

**October 1964**

* **Oct. 28**: Library construction hits another delay when contractor bids arrive more than $100,000 over OWU's cost estimates.
* **Oct. 28**: University officials announce substantial budget cuts and re-budgeting for the next two years to recover from running in the red last year.
* **Oct. 28**: A campus mock election shows President Lyndon B. Johnson leading GOP nominee Barry Goldwater with 52.5% of the student vote.
* **Oct. 28**: *Time* magazine Washington news editor Robert Smith speaks at an assembly political forum regarding news media in the 1964 campaign.
* **Oct. 28**: Former OWU Vice President for University Relations Noel Johnston is inaugurated as the 14th president of Defiance College.
* **Oct. 28**: Wabash spoils OWU's Homecoming with a 21-0 gridiron victory, but soccer defeats Bowling Green 8-2 behind four goals from John Patterson, and cross country defeats Mount Union 23-34.
* **Oct. 28**: Wesleyan Players open their performance season with Jean Anouilh's "The Lark" at Willis Auditorium.

**January 1965**

* **Jan. 13:** Vice President for Academic Affairs Emerson C. Shuck announces that Spring Fever Day will not be held this year.
* **Jan. 13:** Baseball legend Branch Rickey is named national chairman of Ohio Wesleyan's multi-million dollar fund drive.
* **Jan. 13:** The Austin Hall freight elevator crashes to the bottom of its shaft carrying 12 university administrators and Trustees; repairs are completed shortly after.
* **Jan. 13:** A conflict arises between SG President Jim Opfer and Assistant Dean of Men Terence S. Taylor following the Dean's Office ban on MUB cigarette sales.
* **Jan. 13:** Unseasonably good weather allows construction on the new $1.8 million university library to move a week ahead of schedule.
* **Jan. 13:** The first stage of construction on the Delaware bypass/Olentangy River Expressway is completed.
* **Jan. 13:** Former Slater employee Ronald E. Harrison is committed to Lima State Hospital for sanity tests following a Dec. 13 assault on a coed in Monnett Hall.
* **Jan. 13:** OWU announces that Wittenberg will be dropped from the football schedule starting in 1967, ending a 70-year tradition.
* **Jan. 13:** In athletics, freshman Tom Carnes scores 30 points to lead the basketball team over Oberlin 78-59, while the swim team defeats Wooster 67-28.

**April 1965**

* **Apr. 28:** Student leaders present grievances to the Board of Trustees' Student Welfare Committee regarding faculty local autonomy resolutions and fraternity housing rules.
* **Apr. 28:** The Board of Trustees Executive Committee passes a resolution withholding graduation from fraternity men with unpaid room and board bills.
* **Apr. 28:** Dean of Men Ronald S. Stead announces a new policy requiring Greek men to sign housing contracts obligating them to move into Williams Drive fraternity houses if needed to fill quotas.
* **Apr. 28:** *The Transcript* co-managing editor Rog Allaway resigns due to fatigue and academic conflicts.
* **Apr. 28:** Men's Court places eight freshmen on good conduct parole for the remainder of the academic year for firecracker rule violations.
* **Apr. 28:** Bill Buxton is elected Chief Justice of Men's Court, and Dean of Men Ronald S. Stead is named "Boss of the Year" by the local National Secretaries Association chapter.
* **Apr. 28:** Student Government releases its Course Critique, providing course analyses for student registration.
* **Apr. 28:** The Pittsburgh Symphony performs before a near-capacity audience in Gray Chapel.
* **Apr. 28:** The OWU baseball team moves into first place in the Ohio Conference after extending a record-breaking 36-inning unscored-upon streak.

**January 1966**

* **Jan. 12**: Selective Service Director Lt. General Lewis B. Hershey announces that armed forces may draw heavily from college campuses to meet Viet Nam War quotas.
* **Jan. 12**: An Academic Policy Committee subcommittee studies a proposed 3-3-3 plan to eliminate the fall term's fourth course requirement and lower graduation units from 39 to 36.
* **Jan. 12**: Registration proceeds without issue as 2,400 students process through Gray Chapel in four hours.
* **Jan. 12**: Student Senate Chairman Ron Stephany presents a $3,550 check to President Elden T. Smith for the "Thrust Toward Fulfillment" fund drive, an amount subsequently doubled by alumnus Robert E. Eastman ('35).
* **Jan. 12**: Assistant Professor of Psychology Faye Pritchard is elected president of the Faculty Club, becoming the first woman to hold the post.
* **Jan. 12**: Soccer captain Bucky Stultz receives honorable mention on the National Soccer Coaches Association's 1965 All-American team, while the wrestling team dominates Capital 40-4.

**February 1966**

* **Feb. 9**: The Ramsey Lewis Trio kicks off Winter Homecoming weekend with a performance in Gray Chapel, where Le Bijou Queen of 1966 is crowned.
* **Feb. 9**: Registrar Craig D. Willis denies rumors that OWU male students have been drafted into military service.
* **Feb. 9**: An ad hoc court convicts two freshmen of "conduct unbecoming" and begins judging student apartment policy violations.
* **Feb. 9**: The first-term Dean's List includes 351 students, marking a 58 percent increase over the prior year.
* **Feb. 9**: U.S. Senator William Proxmire (D-Wis.) speaks on "The Importance of Politics" as part of Democratic Day events.
* **Feb. 9**: The Coffee House officially opens, attracting over 100 students for folk singing and refreshments.

**November 1966**

* **Nov. 2**: OWU cancels its contract with Slater Food Service, announcing a switch to SAGA Food Service beginning second term.
* **Nov. 2**: The Senior Responsibility Board submits a proposal to end dorm hours for any coed who has attended OWU for three years, regardless of age.
* **Nov. 2**: Alpha Tau Omega signs its local autonomy certificate, making it the final group among OWU's 26 Greek organizations to comply with the university requirement.
* **Nov. 2**: Delaware County Auditor David Thomas refuses to recommend tax exemption for nine Williams Drive fraternity houses, affecting a $58,499.71 appeal by OWU.
* **Nov. 2**: The local chapter of the American Association of University Professors establishes Committee 'S' to investigate student freedom and grievances.
* **Nov. 2**: The OWU sailing team earns a spot as the Midwest representative at the upcoming Sugar Bowl Regatta in New Orleans, while the varsity football team falls 27-0 to Wittenberg.

**January 1967**

* **Jan. 10**: *The Transcript* begins publishing twice weekly on Tuesday and Friday afternoons on a trial basis, replacing its previous Wednesday morning schedule.
* **Jan. 10**: SAGA Food Service takes over dining operations after nine and a half years of Slater Food, earning praise from students.
* **Jan. 10**: OWU hosts over 250 attendees for a conference celebrating 200 years of Methodism in America and OWU's 125th anniversary, awarding three degrees.
* **Jan. 10**: A senior man is suspended after being discovered in the Sigma Phi Epsilon house with a non-student woman.
* **Jan. 10**: Construction continues on OWU's new coed dormitory rising from the Glen, designed to house 235 men and 142 women by fall.
* **Jan. 10**: OWU President Elden T. Smith and Student Government President Woody Clark form a 22-member student-faculty-administrator advisory body to improve campus communication.
* **Jan. 10**: National news hits campus as U.S. Secretary of State Dean Rusk defends Vietnam bombing policies in a letter responding to student leaders, while *Time* magazine names the "New Generation" (25 and under) as its 1966 Man of the Year.
* **Jan. 10**: In sports, the swimming team defeats Wooster 66-38, wrestling beats Capital 31-16 behind five pins, the newly formed hockey club loses its inaugural game 9-6 to Dayton, and basketball falls 80-54 to third-ranked Akron.

**April 1967**

* **Apr. 12**: OWU wins a tax appeal with Delaware County after the deadline passes to appeal the State Board of Tax Appeals decision exempting William Street fraternity land from property taxes.
* **Apr. 12**: U.S. Senator Wayne Morse speaks on campus defending dissent, and syndicated columnist Drew Pearson delivers an address attacking corruption in Congress.
* **Apr. 12**: Men's Court fines Alpha Sigma Phi $300 and places the fraternity on good conduct probation through fall term for liquor violations.
* **Apr. 12**: The Panhellenic Presidents' Council votes to open its meetings to *Transcript* reporters for the first time in its history.
* **Apr. 12**: Admissions Office figures show freshman applications down 11% from the previous year, while construction on the new science building falls 60 days behind schedule.
* **Apr. 12**: Associate Professor of Mathematics David H. Staley is elected president of the OWU chapter of the AAUP.
* **Apr. 12**: Beeghly Library announces plans to send 1,000 books to the University of Malawi in Central Africa under an American Association of Colleges for Teacher Education grant.
* **Apr. 12**: In sports, John Shively sets a Selby Field and OWU record in track, the sailing team wins the University of Detroit Spring Invitational Regatta, tennis defeats Capital 8-1, golf splits its triangular opener against Kenyon and Heidelberg, baseball loses 7-1 to Hiram, and lacrosse drops a match to Kenyon.

**January 1968**
* **Jan. 10**: OWU faces financial pressures due to spiraling college costs, even as total student aid for the 1967–68 academic year reaches a record high near $1 million.
* **Jan. 10**: National draft and civil rights debates touch campus as Yale Chaplain William S. Coffin Jr. expresses delight at his federal indictment for draft counseling, and Fellowship of Reconciliation director Ronald Young is scheduled to lecture on modern revolutions.
* **Jan. 10**: The OWU Hockey Club withdraws from the Midwest Collegiate Hockey Association due to a lack of student participation, while the wrestling team stays undefeated with a 23-14 win over Capital.
* **Jan. 10**: University housing officials order 17 men back into approved housing after finding them in illegal apartments, prompting Chi Phi fraternity to plan the sale of its North Franklin Street property to the University.
* **Jan. 31**: A one-third federal budget cut deprives OWU of over $1 million in expected federal aid approved by the Ohio Board of Regents.
* **Jan. 31**: University Physician Dr. William Henderson resigns, citing the collapse of plans for a new student health center as a factor in his decision.
* **Jan. 31**: Student Council discontinues Student Government Monday chapel assemblies due to lack of interest, while the senior class selects expanding the Beeghly Library book collection as its class gift.
* **Jan. 31**: The Bishop wrestling team advances to 6-1 by defeating Baldwin-Wallace 22-14, and the swimming team defeats Hiram 72-31.

**October 1968**
* **Oct. 9**: *The Transcript* earns All-American honors from the Associated Collegiate Press for its spring semester issues.
* **Oct. 9**: Anti-war critic Dr. Benjamin Spock opens the L-M Series before a capacity crowd in Gray Chapel, as OWU's Vietnam War casualty toll reaches eight following the deaths of three former students over the summer.
* **Oct. 9**: The faculty approves new first-term rush rules following renewed debate over deferred rush, while Student Council passes a measure allowing senior men to live in unapproved housing.
* **Oct. 9**: Plans are finalized for the art department to relocate to the old Delaware Post Office by fall 1969, and Kappa Sigma announces its intent to move into Franklin House.
* **Oct. 9**: The football team defeats Heidelberg 35-7 for its 10th consecutive victory, while the unscored-upon soccer team moves to 2-0 with victories over Bowling Green and Kenyon.

**January 1969**
* **January 8**: Vice-President for Academic Affairs Robert P. Lisensky is named Acting University President by Board of Trustees Chairman Richard Darrow.
* **January 8**: Admissions applications for the Class of 1973 see a 43 percent increase over the previous year.
* **January 8**: The Student Union on Black Awareness (SUBA) publishes "The Black Student At Ohio Wesleyan," while the Student Action Group pushes for curriculum revisions emphasizing Negro culture and achievement.
* **January 8**: Student regulations ease as coeds residing in Austin Hall are permitted to smoke in their rooms and keep cars on campus.
* **January 8**: Eugene Carson Blake is announced as the 1969 Merrick Lecture series speaker, and journalist David Schoenbrun opens the Winter Lecture Series.
* **January 8**: Underground journal *Karma* prepares to publish its second issue.
* **January 8**: In athletics, the men's basketball team defeats Adelbert 108–50 behind a 23-point performance by guard Chip Rosser, while Jim Freeman is named *The Transcript*'s outstanding fall athlete.

**April 1969**
* **April 2**: OWU President-elect Thomas E. Wenzlau, an alumnus and economics professor, visits campus following unanimous trustee approval of a new student apartment lottery policy.
* **April 2**: Federal student loans at OWU face a projected 39 percent reduction for 1969–70; faculty and staff form a special scholarship fund to support incoming needy and black students.
* **April 2**: The Free University program launches with more than 125 students attending inaugural unstructured classes.
* **April 2**: *The Transcript* receives a First Class rating from the Associated Collegiate Press for its previous semester's coverage.
* **April 2**: Associate Professor of Politics and Government Gene Chenoweth resigns to become department chairman at Bucknell University.
* **April 2**: Senior swimmer Doug Andrew earns NCAA College Division All-American honors in the 100-yard backstroke and butterfly, while the OWU baseball team opens its season on the new Littick Field turf.

**January 1970**
* **Jan 7:** R. Philip Shober resigns as vice president for student affairs to return to teaching; Malcolm S. Baroway is named director of public relations.
* **Jan 7:** The fall sports banquet honors 63 lettermen, naming Richard Henley, Small, and John Shively fall MVPs.
* **Jan 14:** The Wesleyan Council on Student Affairs (WCSA) dissolves its controversial 24-hour visitation policy.
* **Jan 14:** The five-year "Thrust Towards Fulfillment" fund-raising campaign concludes, surpassing its $7 million goal by over $63,000.
* **Jan 14:** The Fine Arts Department moves into its new quarters in the old post office on Sandusky Street.
* **Jan 28:** Plans are announced for construction of a $1 million Performing Arts Building to begin in late summer; poet James Dickey appears on campus.
* **Jan 28:** The Academic Policy Committee (APC) presents a new distribution requirement proposal, and a 3.0 GPA requirement is initially adopted for off-campus study.

**February 1970**
* **Feb 18:** The Board of Trustees approves a major structural reorganization of itself and requests a formal review of the university's alcohol policy.
* **Feb 18:** Approximately 80 to 100 students stage a drink-in at Welch dining room in reaction to trustee decisions.
* **Feb 18:** The Cross Cultural Affairs Committee lowers the off-campus study requirement from a "normally 3.00" GPA to a 2.00 prerequisite.
* **Feb 18:** Bishop wrestlers place fourth in the Great Lakes Colleges Association (GLCA) tournament as Peter Earle captures the 118-pound championship.
* **Feb 18:** Rev. Alvin Carmines delivers the 1970 Merrick Lecture in Gray Chapel.

**April 1970**
* **April 8:** University "prohibition" officially ends as a new alcohol policy takes effect in university-owned housing units on April 4.
* **April 8:** OWU receives a $287,000 National Science Foundation grant for college science improvement.
* **April 8:** Georgia State Representative Julian Bond addresses the campus, urging America to reorder its priorities.
* **April 8:** Freshman coeds are granted a no-hours policy for spring term unless parents request otherwise.
* **April 29:** OWU students participate in Earth Day environmental teach-ins and street cleanups across Delaware.
* **April 29:** Edward E. Birch is appointed vice president for student affairs, effective July 15, and the university hires two black professors to join the faculty in the fall.
* **April 29:** The 1905 "Old Grandstand" next to Edwards Gym is razed to clear space for a new gymnasium.

**November 1970**
* **Nov 5:** Ohio state election coverage highlights voter split decision, electing Democrat John J. Gilligan as governor and Republican Robert Taft Jr. to the U.S. Senate.
* **Nov 5:** Former Secretary of the Interior Stewart Udall and pianist Christoph Eschenbach are scheduled for campus appearances.
* **Nov 5:** The OWU sailing team receives a bid to represent the Midwest Collegiate Sailing Association in the Sugar Bowl Regatta.

**January 1971**
* **Jan. 14:** Demonstrators assemble at Gray Chapel to protest Academic Affairs Vice President Robert P. Lisensky's decision not to renew the contract of speech instructor Fred Andrle, sparking broader debate over faculty tenure probation policies.
* **Jan. 14:** U.S. Senator George McGovern speaks at Gray Chapel on "A Second Declaration of Independence" as part of the Lecture-Movie series, while Bernice Reagon delivers a music-lecture on traditional African music in America.
* **Jan. 14:** Fraternity pledging hits a two-year high as 254 freshmen (64% of the class) pledge across OWU's 11 national fraternities.
* **Jan. 14:** The Wesleyan Council on Student Affairs (WCSA) approves Section D of a proposed judicial policy and passes a voluntary signout policy.
* **Jan. 14:** The registrar releases details on a new academic distribution policy, while the Environmental Action Committee begins publishing an ecology newsletter titled *SLIME*.
* **Jan. 14:** OWU opens a new student coffee house called "Roots," featuring musical performances by Phil Gentily and Jack Dunbar, alongside an appearance by the Allman Brothers Band on campus.
* **Jan. 14:** OWU's journalism department receives a $1,000 grant from the Reader's Digest Foundation, while radio station WSLN faces technical delays in starting broadcasts.
* **Jan. 14:** In athletics, soccer goalie Clay Small earns All-American honorable mention; the wrestling team defeats Oberlin (42-0) and Case Western Reserve (23-9); the basketball team falls to Wooster 73-63; and the sailing team finishes 7th at the Sugar Bowl Invitational Regatta.

**April 1971**
* **Jan. 29 / Apr. 29:** OWU students join 350,000 anti-war demonstrators in Washington, D.C., as the campus May Day Committee prepares local anti-war activities.
* **Apr. 29:** The Academic Policy Committee (APC) reviews the Air Force ROTC program curriculum and considers revisions to the Experimental College proposal following faculty critiques.
* **Apr. 29:** The faculty passes a rule requiring academic departments to file official Independent Study policies following reports of course misuse.
* **Apr. 29:** WCSA votes down a motion to incorporate civil law into the proposed Student Code of Conduct.
* **Apr. 29:** Housing Director James Miller announces that 240 students (including 101 women) received permission via lottery to live off-campus next year.
* **Apr. 29:** Senior Robert B. Palmer is arrested at his home and charged on three drug counts, including keeping a house where hallucinogens are kept or sold.
* **Apr. 29:** Andy Young wins a runoff election for Graduating Class Trustee, while total university gift fund revenue drops by $30,000 despite a major $125,000 donation.
* **Apr. 29:** In sports, OWU sailors win the Ohio State Invitational—the largest intercollegiate regatta in U.S. history—led by Athlete of the Week Fritz Hanselman.
* **Apr. 29:** The lacrosse team edges Oberlin 10-9; the tennis team places 3rd at the Great Lakes Championships; and the track team takes 4th place at the GLCA meet at Wabash.

**January 1972**
- **Jan 20**: Over 1,400 students petition the faculty to reconsider eliminating distribution requirements; a new "Theater Board" is elected for the Chappelear Drama Center transition; and cigarette machines return to dorms and the Union following a seven-year ban.
- **Jan 20**: Radical attorney William M. Kunstler speaks on American justice in Gray Chapel, while two outside consultants urge retaining social welfare classes.
- **Jan 20**: Academic VP Robert Lisensky denies rumors of taking the presidency at West Virginia Wesleyan; eight faculty members announce plans to retire in June; and former copy editor Linda McCullough resigns from *The Transcript*.
- **Jan 20**: In athletics, swimmer Jackie Brown earns Athlete of the Week, OWU aquamen defeat Muskingum 77-30, and the wrestling team pushes its win streak to 17 meets.

**October 1972**
- **Oct 05**: An exclusive *Transcript* poll shows OWU students backing President Richard Nixon 2-to-1 over Sen. George McGovern, while local McGovern offices open in Delaware and Young Socialist Alliance members campaign on campus.
- **Oct 05**: Syndicated columnist Art Buchwald opens the Lecture-Artist Series in Gray Chapel, and guitarist Muddy Waters is announced to headline the Social Committee program.
- **Oct 05**: The administration rejects WCSA's proposal to merge Homecoming and Dad's Day, while Ohio Wesleyan becomes the GLCA agent for the New York Fine Arts program.
- **Oct 05**: In sports, football running back Jim Michals is named Athlete of the Week after leading OWU to a 41-6 win over Grove City, while Dayton snaps the soccer team's 12-game unbeaten streak.

**January 1973**
* **Jan. 11**: The Union's Joint Task Force submits a $150,000 remodeling proposal to the Trustees, recommending an enlarged snack bar, rathskeller, student office space, and the legalization of alcohol in the Union.
* **Jan. 11**: Faculty grants final approval to the Student Code of Conduct following extensive debate.
* **Jan. 11**: Assistant Professor of Sociology Thomas Brittenham gains tenure following a three-month appeal process.
* **Jan. 11**: Senior Christopher S. Little, 23, dies in Columbus, Ohio, from injuries sustained in a two-story fall.
* **Jan. 11**: Senior Jeff Knox is revealed to be the target of a kidnapping hoax over Christmas break.
* **Jan. 11**: Fifty students, faculty, and local residents meet to plan anti-war demonstrations for Inauguration weekend.
* **Jan. 11**: OWU receives a donation of Moral Re-Armament (MRA) memorabilia, placing the university in position to become MRA national headquarters.
* **Jan. 11**: WCSA unanimously passes judiciary reforms, eliminating the Court of Five and streamlining the judicial system.
* **Jan. 11**: Former football coach Glenn Fraser returns to coach varsity tennis, while soccer and lacrosse coach Fred Myers resumes work after recovering from a November heart attack.
* **Jan. 11**: The basketball team wins two of three games at the Great Lakes Classic after losing its first five games in December.

**April 1973**
* **April 5**: Delaware County Prosecutor Henry Shaw files a lawsuit against OWU to recover $12,357.33 in unpaid personal property taxes accumulated by the bookstore since 1960.
* **April 5**: The faculty votes down a WCSA proposal that sought to add a student member to the Faculty Personnel Committee.
* **April 5**: Air Force ROTC Commander Major Stanley Voyiaziakis receives verbal notice that the unit will remain at OWU until at least June 1976.
* **April 5**: *The Washington Merry-Go-Round* columnist Jack Anderson is scheduled to address the university at Gray Chapel.
* **April 5**: A $20 board fee increase to $600 is proposed for Trustee approval ahead of the next academic year.
* **April 5**: Thieves steal over $500 in cash and merchandise from university property at Christian House during spring break.
* **April 5**: *The Transcript* receives its third consecutive First Class Honors rating from the Associated Collegiate Press.
* **April 5**: Sophomores Bob Argo and Jim O'Conner establish the Pre-Medical Association.
* **April 5**: OWU athletic squads launch spring action: lacrosse edges Kenyon 11-10 in overtime, rugby shuts out Findlay 42-0, and track splits its opening meet against Muskingum and Wittenberg.

**November 1973**
* **November 22**: Admissions Director David Treadwell reports a 28% drop in admissions applications, down to 252 from 323 the previous year.
* **November 22**: The university's Air Force ROTC unit faces an Air Force review with termination recommended, pending a final decision in the spring.
* **November 22**: Assistant Professor of English Herschel Shohan declines to appeal his tenure denial by the Faculty Personnel Committee and will depart after his contract ends.
* **November 22**: The Chaplain's Office closes the Coffeehouse at 56 University Ave. due to declining student interest and lack of organizational direction.
* **November 22**: Student directors at WSLN radio unanimously propose transferring station oversight from the speech department to the journalism department.
* **November 22**: The soccer team finishes as runner-up in the Midwest Liberal Arts Soccer Invitational and earns top honors in the Ohio Conference from league coaches.
* **November 22**: Gridder Duane Petty is named Athlete of the Term after setting an outstanding pass interception record.
* **November 22**: Twenty-six sophomores are inducted into the Phi Society in recognition of high academic achievement.

**January 1974**
- **Jan. 10**: The faculty approves next year's academic calendar featuring a six-week break and requests that the administration review potential sex discrimination regarding female faculty salaries.
- **Jan. 10**: U.S. Sen. Howard Baker (R-Tenn.), vice-chairman of the Senate Watergate Committee, speaks in Gray Chapel as part of the Lecture-Artist Series.
- **Jan. 10**: Energy and gas shortages affect student travel and prompt energy-saving directives on campus, though Catering Management Incorporated (CMI) confirms food services will not be cut back.
- **Jan. 10**: A target date of June 30 is set to reach the $2 million needed to build a new physical education center and renovate Edwards Gym.
- **Jan. 10**: Ohio Wesleyan receives a $6,000 grant from the Martha Holden Jennings Foundation to create a freshman colloquia program with Delaware Hayes High School.
- **Jan. 10**: A U.S. Supreme Court ruling broadens police search powers during minor arrests.
- **Jan. 10**: In sports, eleven fall athletes earn All-Midwest, All-Ohio, or All-Conference honors, while the basketball team drops a 63-61 decision to Kenyon.

**May 1974**
- **May 23**: The Academic Policy Committee unanimously approves 19 arts-professional programs for full faculty consideration.
- **May 23**: The Board of Trustees votes 23-7 to reject a WCSA proposal to allow 3.2 percent beer in the Student Union and announces honorary degree recipients.
- **May 23**: Air Force ROTC leaves Ohio Wesleyan after 25 years, while campus security guards begin carrying nightsticks following multiple physical assaults.
- **May 23**: A new financial aid program emphasizing loans and work grants is estimated to save the university $125,000 annually.
- **May 23**: Former U.S. Attorney General Elliot Richardson, novelist Robert Penn Warren, and the Cincinnati Symphony are announced for the upcoming Lecture-Artist Series.
- **May 23**: Associate Professor of English Robert Flanagan receives a $5,000 fiction grant from the National Endowment for the Arts.
- **May 23**: Campus groups lead a fundraising drive to aid drought victims in Africa and assist Wilberforce University following tornado damage in Xenia.
- **May 23**: In athletics, the lacrosse team falls 13-11 to Bowling Green in the Midwest Lacrosse Association championship, while sophomore George Saunders is named Athlete of the Year for his achievements in soccer and tennis.

**January 1975**

* **Jan. 16**: The Board of Trustees and faculty approve the Ohio Wesleyan-Riverside Hospital baccalaureate nursing program.
* **Jan. 16**: University officials anticipate next year's budget cuts will reach $500,000 amid a 14% drop in admissions applications.
* **Jan. 16**: President Thomas Wenzlau announces that contract signing for the new gymnasium complex is imminent.
* **Jan. 16**: English professor Herschel Shohan unexpectedly resigns, citing departmental secrecy regarding his contract status.
* **Jan. 16**: The Wesleyan Council on Student Affairs (WCSA) votes 10-8 to allow the Interfraternity Council to run its own rush and pledging investigations.
* **Jan. 16**: Professional Dining Service (PDS) takes over campus food operations from Catering Management Incorporated (CMI).
* **Jan. 16**: Installation of a new direct-dial phone system in Smith Hall reaches 85% completion.
* **Jan. 16**: OWU receives a $30,000 National Endowment for the Humanities grant for Greek culture courses and a $1,000 Reader's Digest grant for the journalism department.
* **Jan. 16**: Senior Terry Tewanger dies at University Hospital in Columbus from complications due to a rare blood disease.
* **Jan. 16**: Eugene White is elected president of OWU's chapter of the American Association of University Professors.

**March 1975**

* **March 6**: The Publications Board votes unanimously to recommend discontinuing *Le Bijou* after this year due to poor yearbook sales.
* **March 6**: OWU approves an experimental $17,500 no-need scholarship program starting next year, while raising the student activity fee to $13.
* **March 6**: Assistant professor of journalism F. O. Wellnitz becomes the sixth full-time faculty member cut for the upcoming academic year.
* **March 6**: Eight of ten department chairmen surveyed by *The Transcript* confirm that grade inflation and declining academic standards exist at OWU.

* **Sept. 15:** Douglas Steeples assumes office as OWU's new Provost.
* **Sept. 15:** The 1984-85 Fiske Selective Guide to Colleges awards Ohio Wesleyan three stars for academics.
* **Sept. 15:** Football opens its season with a 17-17 tie against Kenyon College.
* **Sept. 15:** Ohio Wesleyan receives its fifth OAC Commissioner's Trophy as all-sports champion for the preceding academic year.

**January 1984**
* **Jan. 12**: The Board of Trustees prepares to select Ohio Wesleyan's next president from two top candidates—David Warren, chief administrative officer for New Haven, Conn., and Wayne Anderson, president of Maryville College—as outgoing President Thomas Wenzlau departs for Colorado College.
* **Jan. 12**: A severe gas leak outside Smith Hall forces the overnight evacuation of approximately 105 Smith Hall West residents.
* **Jan. 12**: Sophomore John Bell recovers at Grady Hospital after being mugged and knocked unconscious near Sanborn.
* **Jan. 12**: Housing figures show campus vacancies at 250, with projections reaching over 400 for the following year, while early decision applications drop 28 percent.
* **Jan. 12**: Student radio station WSLN (98.7 FM) resumes broadcasting following six weeks of transmitter troubles.
* **Jan. 12**: The Academic Policy Committee sends a proposed policy on repeating failed courses back to subcommittee.
* **Jan. 12**: In sports, line-backer Eric DiMartino earns Kodak All-America honors, men's basketball improves to 9-4 with a 98-54 win over Kenyon, and Tracy Moritz wins the overall springboard competition in a swim meet loss to Ohio Northern.

**April 1984**
* **April 12**: Faculty members approve a pilot for the National Colloquium Speaker Series focusing on the nuclear age, with President David Warren seeking outside funding for the program.
* **April 12**: The Rev. Norman Vincent Peale ('20) is announced as the commencement speaker for June 10.
* **April 12**: Greek Affairs Coordinator Rob Keith resigns, drawing 20 applicants for the opening post.
* **April 12**: Admissions reports total applications trail the previous year by 8.5 percent, with acceptances down 15 percent.
* **April 12**: Actor Richard Kiley brings his one-man show, *Verse Person Singular*, to Gray Chapel.
* **April 12**: Around 750 high school students gather at Branch Rickey Center for State Science Day, while public safety investigates the theft of nine trees valued at over $1,500.
* **April 12**: In athletics, the women's track team captures the GLCA title, the men's track team wins the sprint medley at the Otterbein Relays, and senior Clint Mabie leads the golf team to victory at the Marietta Invitational.

**September 1984**
* **September 27**: Public Safety Director William Sexton leaves his post amid conflicting statements from administration regarding whether he resigned or was suspended.
* **September 27**: Preparations wrap up for the inauguration of President David Warren on Sept. 29 in Gray Chapel, as Warren plans to resume his "live-in presidency" in Bashford Hall.
* **September 27**: WCSA approves new residence hall security procedures requiring students to present OWU identification when entering dorms after 11 p.m.
* **September 27**: The National Colloquium Speaker Series features discussions on atomic bomb imagery and nuclear culture.
* **September 27**: In sports, the 6th-ranked men's soccer team defeats rival Denison 2-1 at Roy Rike Field, field hockey blanks Hiram 3-0, and the football team falls 17-12 to Kenyon.

**February 1985**
* **Feb. 1**: Provost Douglas Steeples resigns, effective June 30, 1985. Professor William Louthan is appointed executive assistant to the University president.
* **Feb. 1**: Rumors regarding a campus drug investigation create tension between Dean of Student Services Larry Mangus and local fraternity presidents.
* **Feb. 1**: Cleveland contractor Elmer Benes pledges $1 million to Ohio Wesleyan following a near fall down the stairs in the Alumni Relations Office.
* **Feb. 1**: Football players Bob Hill, Dean Cordle, and Dean Hood are named to the 1984 Pizza Hut Division III All-America team.
* **Feb. 8**: The city of Delaware considers purchasing Edgar Hall, while the Board of Trustees meets to consider 1985–86 student fees and plans for Austin Hall.
* **Feb. 8**: The campus judicial board investigates the College Republican Club's finances, including over $80 unaccounted for by club president James Paquette.
* **Feb. 8**: Phi Beta Kappa votes to exclude juniors from election, breaking a 77-year campus tradition.
* **Feb. 8**: Head football coach Steve Farkasovsky signs a new three-year contract, while the women's track team captures the NCAC relay title.

**March 1985**
* **March 29**: University President David Warren and donor Elmer Benes break ground on the $1 million Frances E. Mowry Alumni Center, with construction set for May.
* **March 29**: WCSA approves a new three-level student judicial structure, but rejects continuing the trial "Campus Loop" safety ride van program.
* **March 29**: The romance languages living group loses its facility to the peace and justice group after failing to meet its 15-resident quota.
* **March 29**: National Colloquium coordinator Richard Elias announces he will leave Ohio Wesleyan at the end of the academic year.
* **March 29**: Public safety officials report no leads in the third week following the theft of a 19th-century painting from Beeghly Library.
* **March 29**: Junior swimmer John Madden earns All-America honors in the 100-yard breaststroke at the NCAA Division III Championships.

**October 1985**
* **March 4/Oct. 4**: The Board of Trustees approves divestment from South Africa and increases internal risk investments to address a $1,324,000 annual deficit.
* **Oct. 4**: Interfraternity Council President Charlie Engeman submits witness evidence to Provost Larry Wilson supporting fraternity charges against Dean Larry Mangus.
* **Oct. 4**: University officials launch an investigation into $313.77 worth of illegal long-distance telephone fraud logged during the first week of classes.
* **Oct. 4**: Physical plant staff begin digging an energy cost-cutting tunnel linking Beeghly Library and Chappelear Drama Center.
* **Oct. 4**: Fall fraternity rush concludes with 104 men pledging, while Alpha Phi Alpha secures a new chapter room in Bashford Hall.
* **Oct. 4**: Campus organizers schedule "Apartheid Alert" events, and author Wendell Berry arrives for a two-week campus residency.
* **Oct. 4**: The women's soccer team earns its first-ever varsity victory.

**January 1986**
* **Jan. 24:** G. William Benz is selected as OWU's next provost effective June 1; economist John Kenneth Galbraith is named commencement speaker; Mike Pressler is named head lacrosse coach; MLK Jr. Day receives its first national observance with memorial events on campus.
* **Jan. 31:** Board of Trustees adopts the "Growth Model" strategic plan and raises general fees 9.3% to $11,915; Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity is cleared of harassment charges; *The Transcript* debuts the syndicated comic strip *Bloom County*.

**February 1986**
* **Feb. 7:** National Colloquium (UC 50) enrollment declines 50%, prompting administrative review.
* **Feb. 14:** Students face $10 fines for unapproved telephone extensions in dorm rooms; Hug-a-thon '86 raises funds for battered wives.
* **Feb. 21:** Vice President of Business Affairs Bob Meyer announces May retirement after 38 years; eight small living units are granted housing; Robert Fernandez is appointed editor of *The Transcript*.
* **Feb. 28:** Men's basketball captures its second straight NCAC tournament title; Beth Vietze wins the graduating class trustee election; faculty approve a revised campus alcohol policy.

**March 1986**
* **March 7:** WCSA approves revised judicial codes; Cager Scott Tedder is named NCAC Player of the Year, and Nan Carney-Debord is named NCAC Women's Basketball Coach of the Year.
* **March 28:** Haitian Seminar students travel to Haiti despite political unrest; Robert J. Brant is named director of residential life; swimmer John Vaughan earns All-America honors at NCAA Division III nationals.

**April 1986**
* **April 4:** Journalism department chairman Verne Edwards announces early retirement; Julie MacMillan is elected WCSA student body president.
* **April 11:** Senior class president candidates debate live on WSLN radio; a $500 writing award is established in memory of Helen Beal Woodward ('35).
* **April 18:** Dave Lavenburg wins the senior class presidency in a runoff; Interfraternity Council votes unanimously to reinstate Beta Theta Pi.
* **April 25:** Earth Day activities draw over 2,700 participants; faculty narrow-margin vote approves "Private lives - public issues" as the National Colloquium IV topic.

**September 1986**
* **Sept. 5:** Freshman enrollment jumps 43%; Donald Chenoweth replaces Larry Mangus as dean of student services; the English Language Program is scheduled to terminate in December following the death of director Barbara Mallett; former U.S. Attorney General Ramsay Clark opens the National Colloquium.
* **Sept. 12:** Delaware police arrest six OWU students at the Brown Jug Restaurant; Louis Szalontai takes office as vice president for business affairs.
* **Sept. 19:** Wabash defeats the young Bishop football team 52-0 in the home opener.
* **Sept. 26:** Trustees approve an additional 4% faculty salary hike (totaling 6%) after enrollment exceeds expectations; WSLN begins broadcasting in stereo.

**October 1986**
* **Oct. 3:** The Center for Economics and Business opens in Edgar Hall; soccer player Brian Bundy becomes OWU's all-time leading scorer.
* **Oct. 10:** Beeghly Library celebrates its 20th anniversary; human rights lectures address state torture in Chile.
* **Oct. 17:** Five South African OWU students express support for U.S. congressional sanctions against South Africa; poet Denise Levertov begins her residency as Carpenter Lecturer.
* **Oct. 24:** Ohio Governor Richard Celeste appoints President David Warren to lead a high school exchange program to the Soviet Union; men's soccer clinches the NCAC title.

**November 1986**
* **Nov. 7:** A water main leak prompts a citywide water emergency in Delaware; a six-point buck crashes through the Smith Hall dining room window; Phi Kappa Psi is placed on alcohol probation.
* **Nov. 14:** Communications expert Neil Postman speaks at the National Colloquium; football completes a winless season; men's soccer advances to the NCAA Division III quarterfinals.

**December 1986**
* **Dec. 5:** Head football coach Steve Farkasovsky resigns; former President Gerald Ford is confirmed as an upcoming National Colloquium speaker; two Japanese economists visit campus for the "Japan Project."

**January 1987**
* **Jan 23:** OWU students and faculty join Rev. Jesse Jackson and Coretta Scott King for a civil rights march in Forsyth County, Georgia.
* **Jan 23:** Mike Hollway is named head football coach following the resignation of Steve Farkasovsky.
* **Jan 23:** Faculty express concern that Pew Grant implementation for the National Colloquium bypassed proper committee channels.
* **Jan 30:** The Board of Trustees votes to increase tuition, room, and board by 8 percent to $12,868 for the next academic year.
* **Jan 30:** A national search begins for a Dean of Student Services, while Beta Theta Pi reaches its 20-member requirement to discuss regaining its house.

**February 1987**
* **Feb 6:** A CIA recruitment visit sparks a faculty teach-in in the MUB lobby.
