* **Feb 6:** A fire at campus radio station WSLN cuts off the men's basketball broadcast.
* **Feb 13:** U.S. Sen. Joseph Biden speaks in Gray Chapel as part of the National Colloquium.
* **Feb 20:** Men's basketball clinches the North Coast Athletic Conference (NCAC) title with an 81-71 win over Case Western Reserve.
* **Feb 27:** Beta Theta Pi officially regains its former house at 9 Williams Dr.
* **Feb 27:** British band Squeeze cancels its scheduled April 17 campus concert.

**March 1987**
* **March 25:** U.S. Rep. Pat Schroeder addresses the National Colloquium in Branch Rickey Arena.
* **March 25:** A $40,000 Steinway piano is accidentally pushed off the stage during preparations for the OWU Star Search, forcing the event's postponement.
* **March 25:** John Smitson is elected senior class trustee for the Class of 1987.

**April 1987**
* **April 1:** Men's lacrosse defeats seven-time defending champion Hobart 7-4, earning the No. 1 Division III ranking.
* **April 15:** Julie MacMillan is elected student body president; WSLN temporarily shuts down due to staff equipment abuse and missed shifts.
* **April 22:** Former President Gerald Ford delivers the keynote address in Gray Chapel for Constitution Day.
* **April 24:** Otis Day and the Knights perform a concert in Branch Rickey Arena.

**August 1987**
* **Aug 27:** Fall enrollment reaches a record high exceeding 1,600 students.
* **Aug 27:** James P. Pitts is appointed new Dean of Academic Affairs, and Jef Zeigler takes over as Director of Campus Programs.

**September 1987**
* **Sept 2:** IFC President Dan Gibbons refuses to resign following fraternity rush alcohol violations on The Hill.
* **Sept 16:** Greek rush concludes with 300 total pledges (189 men, 111 women); 13 students face charges for using fake IDs at United Dairy Farmers.
* **Sept 23:** Radio station WSLN resumes broadcasting from Slocum Hall.
* **Sept 30:** President David Warren signs a contract extension keeping him at OWU through June 1992.

**October 1987**
* **Oct 7:** The football team shuts out Case Western Reserve 22-0; OWU inducts 12 members into its Athletic Hall of Fame during Fallfest.
* **Oct 14:** A broken steamline cuts heat to the main academic campus; a six-foot Haitian boa constrictor missing since spring is recovered.
* **Oct 21:** Men's soccer earns the No. 1 ranking in Division III.
* **Oct 28:** Field hockey clinches its first NCAC title; residential staff begin distributing condoms in dormitories to promote safe sex.

**November 1987**
* **Nov 4:** Dean of Student Services Don Chenoweth halts the distribution of fraternity T-shirts featuring offensive slogans, sparking free speech debates.
* **Nov 11:** The football team finishes its best season since 1971 by defeating Wittenberg 21-12.
* **Nov 18:** Men's soccer falls 1-0 to Washington (Mo.) in the Great Lakes Regional final, ending its national championship run.
* **Nov 18:** Lee Williams is elected president of the Interfraternity Council.

**December 1987**
* **Dec 9:** OWU announces a partnership with Columbus businessman Arthur Kobacker to offer enrollment incentives to needy youth.
* **Dec 9:** Artist Ebb Haycock receives a commission to create the campus's first outdoor sculpture.
* **Dec 9:** Scott Tedder scores 40 points, but men's basketball drops a 98-87 contest to Capital.

**January 1988**
* **Jan. 18:** The third annual King Celebration is held at Willis Junior High School to pay tribute to Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
* **Jan. 18:** President David Warren announces renovations at Austin Hall and addresses campus parking concerns during a faculty meeting.
* **Jan. 20:** Cable 10 temporary television studio begins programming under assistant professor Michael Murrie.
* **Jan. 20:** Maintenance superintendent Duane Knecht reports a Dec. 15 wind storm caused $12,500 in campus damage.
* **Jan. 20:** First-year head football coach Mike Hollway ties for 8th place for Ohio Coach of the Year.

**February 1988**
* **Feb. 3:** *The Transcript* resumes publication after being halted by printing debt.
* **Feb. 3:** Kathryn Ogletree is appointed as the new adviser for minority students.
* **Feb. 5:** The Board of Trustees accepts a $1 million donation designated for a new student center on University Avenue.
* **Feb. 10:** The men's basketball team climbs to 4th in the national Division III poll after taking the NCAC lead.
* **Feb. 25:** Senior Donna Martino is elected senior class trustee.

**March 1988**
* **March 16:** Junior Steve Payne is named editor of *The Transcript*.
* **March 23:** The men's basketball team wins the NCAA Division III National Championship, defeating Scranton 92-70 to finish 27-5.
* **March 23:** Seven women swimmers achieve All-America honors at the NCAA Division III Championship meet.
* **March 23:** The Health and Fitness House and Women's House are approved as new small living units for the upcoming academic year.
* **March 30:** James Foley wins a runoff election against Derek Haught for student body president.

**April 1988**
* **April 6:** Delta Zeta is selected to establish a new sorority chapter on campus.
* **April 6:** Men's basketball coach Gene Mehaffey is named Division III Coach of the Year, and senior Scott Tedder is named Division III Player of the Year.
* **April 13:** U.S. Senator Howard Metzenbaum serves as keynote speaker for the OWU Mock Convention.
* **April 13:** *The Transcript* ends its publication year early due to accumulated debt.

**August 1988**
* **Aug. 23:** The incoming freshman class registers its highest selectivity level in 20 years.
* **Aug. 23:** The women's track team captures the NCAC outdoor championship with a record 209 points, while men's lacrosse finishes as national runner-up to Hobart.
* **Aug. 24:** National Colloquium V opens with keynote speaker Dick Enberg addressing "Sport, Culture, and Public Values."
* **Aug. 24:** Jon Powers assumes duties as the new campus chaplain.

**September 1988**
* **Sept. 7:** Former Olympic gold medalist Donna de Varona lectures on women in sports as part of the National Colloquium.
* **Sept. 15:** Dr. Harry Edwards delivers a National Colloquium address on racial discrimination in athletics.
* **Sept. 23:** Students Bill Kroener, Jeff Eddy, and Jay Riesz die from injuries sustained in an automobile accident in Lorain County.
* **Sept. 28:** An OWU trustee pledges $1 million to the university during the fall board meeting.

**October 1988**
* **Oct. 5:** Ebb Haycock's sculpture "Oracle" is installed in front of Beeghly Library as OWU's first permanent outdoor sculpture, and Arthur Ashe receives the first Branch Rickey Award.
* **Oct. 12:** An anti-apartheid shanty is erected near the Women's House to protest university investments in South Africa.
* **Oct. 22:** Unrest occurs on campus following the burning of a cross in front of the anti-apartheid shanty.
* **Oct. 26:** A campus poll reveals 57% support for Republican candidate George Bush over Democrat Michael Dukakis (28%) in the upcoming presidential race.

**November 1988**
* **Nov. 8:** Vice President George Bush wins the U.S. presidential election.
* **Nov. 9:** Botany professor Jane Decker dies at age 53 following a battle with cancer.
* **Nov. 12:** Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity celebrates its centennial anniversary at Ohio Wesleyan.
* **Nov. 16:** Academic Affairs Dean James Pitts is chosen to represent the U.S. at the U.S.-USSR Emerging Leaders Summit.

**December 1988**
* **Dec. 7:** Three students receive December Wesleyan Winner honors for their quick response following the October cross-burning incident.
* **Dec. 7:** Sportswriter Frank Deford presents "The Media and the Athletes" for the National Colloquium speaker series.

**January 1989**
* **Jan. 17**: The campus mourns the death of student, track athlete, and Phi Delta Theta member Thomas Britton Schultz, holding a memorial service in Gray Chapel. The OWU community also expresses grief over the 35 Syracuse University students lost in the Pan Am Flight 103 bombing.

**February 1989**
* **Feb. 1**: Investigators confirm a bomb in cargo luggage destroyed Pan Am Flight 103.
* **Feb. 1**: A Lorain County trial is set for March 15 for Sherry Welker, charged in the traffic accident that killed three OWU students.
* **Feb. 1**: Fundraising begins for a $9.5 million student center alongside ongoing renovations to Welch Hall.
* **Feb. 1**: Soviet artist and poet Dmitri Prigov arrives at OWU for an artist-in-residence program.
* **Feb. 1**: Politics and government professor Dr. Carl Pinkele meets PLO leader Yassir Arafat during a faculty tour in Saudi Arabia.
* **Feb. 1**: Men's basketball head coach Gene Mehaffey secures his 399th career victory with a 97-74 win over Case Western Reserve.

**March 1989**
* **March 29**: Sherry Welker pleads guilty to all charges in the fatal crash that killed three OWU juniors.
* **March 29**: University President David Warren, Provost William Benz, and Vice President Robert Holm join the steering committee for OWU's $50 million capital campaign.
* **March 29**: H. Lee Williams wins the run-off election for graduating class trustee.
* **March 29**: OWU selects "The Impact of Technology on Culture" as the theme for the 1989–90 National Colloquium.
* **March 29**: Campus hosts Women's Week and AIDS Awareness Day events, including discussions on controversial texts like *The Satanic Verses*.
* **March 29**: Both the men's and women's track teams capture North Coast Athletic Conference (NCAC) indoor championship titles.

**September 1989**
* **Sept. 13**: A 7 percent enrollment increase leads to tight housing accommodations across campus dormitories.
* **Sept. 13**: Fraternity and sorority rush open concurrently, with fraternity rush starting a week later in the term than past years.
* **Sept. 13**: The University sets a $1.9 million annual fund goal for the 1989–90 academic year following an $1.8 million result the prior year.
* **Sept. 13**: The English Department condenses freshman English requirements.
* **Sept. 13**: The OWU Habitat for Humanity chapter begins its first hands-on work project.
* **Sept. 13**: Football opens its season with a 23-12 victory over Otterbein.

**October 1989**
* **Oct. 25**: Delaware County activates its new 911 emergency response system, granting campus access.
* **Oct. 25**: Cable television outlets are installed across dormitories as subscriptions open to students.
* **Oct. 25**: Administration and WCSA review a proposal for a new computer microlab in Slocum Hall.
* **Oct. 25**: Sophomore Gunendra Sellahewa establishes a campus Buddhist group to unite students in worship.
* **Oct. 25**: A Fallfest flyer distributed by Students Against Apartheid depicting the Battling Bishop binding a slave sparks campus debate over OWU investments in South Africa.
* **Oct. 25**: Football defeats Wabash 20-8 to move to 5th in the Division III North Region, while field hockey advances to a 10-0 NCAC record.

**January 1990**
* **Jan. 17:** Faculty unanimously passes a motion recommending that the Board of Trustees divest investments in companies operating in South Africa.
* **Jan. 17:** The Community Service House at 62 University Ave. is demolished to clear land for foundation work on the new Campus Center.
* **Jan. 17:** University President David Warren is elected chair of the NCAA Presidents Commission for Division III colleges.
* **Jan. 17:** An anonymous donor pledges a $300,000 challenge grant to renovate Selby Stadium.
* **Jan. 17:** Humanities professor Donald Lateiner publishes his first book, focusing on ancient Greek historian Herodotus.

**February 1990**
* **Feb. 14:** WCSA moves to clarify alcohol policies with administration; author Valora Washington lectures on Affirmative Action for Black History Month.
* **Feb. 28:** Five separate charges are filed against Alpha Tau Omega regarding events during pre-initiation week.
* **Feb. 28:** Five OWU students depart for a 12-day educational trip to the Soviet Union.
* **Feb. 28:** Women's basketball reaches the NCAC tournament semifinals, concluding their season with 17 victories.

**March 1990**
* **Mar. 28:** State Liquor Control agents and Delaware Police arrest nine OWU students during simultaneous raids at the Backstretch and West End bars.
* **Mar. 28:** Alumnus Thomas Root is indicted by a federal grand jury on 33 counts of fraud.
* **Mar. 28:** Elizabeth Phillips wins re-election as WCSA President alongside Vice President Doug Nowacek.
* **Mar. 28:** Varsity baseball opens with a doubleheader sweep over Capital University (5-1, 6-5).

**April 1990**
* **April 4:** The Kresge Foundation awards a $500,000 challenge grant toward completing the Hamilton-Williams Campus Center.
* **April 4:** Women lead a "Take Back the Night" march and discussion protesting sexual assault and rape.
* **April 18:** Protesters light a series of fires on Fraternity Hill following the confiscation and theft of six kegs from the public safety storeroom.
* **April 18:** Police and postal authorities intercept a package of marijuana addressed to an off-campus student.

**August 1990**
* **Aug. 23:** OWU completes divestment from South Africa, prompting students to remove the shanty from the Slocum Hall lawn.
* **Aug. 23:** Elliott Hall renovation nears completion following a $1 million alumni gift.
* **Aug. 23:** Incoming transfer student Robert Fraser dies in an automobile accident.

**September 1990**
* **Sep. 12:** Battling Bishop football opens its season with a 27-0 shutout victory against Hiram College.
* **Sep. 12:** Environmental and Wildlife Organization places new recycling bins across campus.
* **Sep. 26:** An OWU alumnus credited with discovering ozone layer depletion speaks at the National Colloquium.
* **Sep. 26:** Students hold a "Do or Die Day" rally opposing Supreme Court nominee David Souter; football shuts out Wooster 41-0.

**October 1990**
* **Oct. 24:** Elliott Hall is officially rededicated by President Warren and alumni donors.
* **Oct. 24:** New exterior lighting is installed on Fraternity Hill to replace fixtures destroyed in April.
* **Oct. 31:** Safety whistles are distributed to all female students, faculty, and staff; students launch the "Safewatch" volunteer escort service.
* **Oct. 31:** Football suffers a 14-10 loss to Allegheny, ending its NCAC championship contention.

**December 1990**
* **Dec. 12:** The university community celebrates the holidays with Christmas caroling and the lighting of the Slocum Walkway of Trees.
* **Dec. 12:** Politics professor William Louthan publishes a book on the U.S. Supreme Court.
* **Dec. 12:** Gospel Lyres choir presents its 18th annual Winter Festival concert in Gray Chapel.

**February 1991**
* Feb. 7: Ohio Wesleyan celebrates Black History Month with activities organized by the Student Union on Black Awareness (SUBA) and Sister's United.
* Feb. 7: University administrators secure a $1 million interest-free advance from food service contractor Marriott Corp. to cover unexpected construction costs for the Hamilton-Williams Campus Center.
* Feb. 7: Sigma Phi Epsilon hosts the first stop of OWU's Trustees Progressive Dinner.
* Feb. 7: Men's basketball earns NCAC victories against Earlham and Case Western Reserve behind strong performances from seniors Dale Eilrich, Dirk Miller, and Sam Hiles.

**March 1991**
* March 21: Twenty-three students and two faculty members travel to Sumpter, South Carolina over spring break to build houses with Habitat for Humanity.
* March 21: A proposal to introduce a plus-minus grading scale (B+=3.3, B=3.0, B-=2.67) is presented to faculty, WCSA, and students.
* March 21: Chi Phi fraternity hosts its annual Bedraces to raise funds for the National Multiple Sclerosis Society.
* March 21: Junior Keith Rucker wins the NCAA Division III indoor shot put title, while the women's swimming squad places 20th in the nation at the NCAA championship meet.

**April 1991**
* April 24: Black students express outrage over a *Transcript* article covering a drug investigation involving Public Safety officer Eric Wright.
* April 24: The OWU Rugby Club is banned from hosting its remaining home matches following charges of misconduct.
* April 24: Women's track athletes McNamara and Althoff qualify for the NCAA Division III National Championships, while head women's lacrosse coach Mary Parker and head field hockey coach Nan Carney-DeBord resign from their respective coaching roles.
* April 24: Austin Manor residents face telephone cutoffs following an academic year of University billing glitches.

**September 1991**
* Sept. 11: OWU President David Warren and Dr. David Hamilton Smith participate in the official ribbon-cutting dedication of the Hamilton-Williams Campus Center.
* Sept. 11: WCSA President Dan Sellers secretly places a condom inside the campus center's commemorative time capsule.
* Sept. 11: OWU considers closing the Riverside School of Nursing, sparking faculty and student efforts to preserve the program.
* Sept. 11: Head coach Linda Strapp wins her field hockey debut in a 4-0 shutout against Oberlin.

**October 1991**
* Oct. 16: An OWU professor gains national media attention after discovering Earth's oldest organism.
* Oct. 16: The Delaware police department shuts down an alcohol- and drug-free party hosted by the House of Spirituality due to noise complaints.
* Oct. 16: Friends and faculty memorialize 1991 graduate Susan Conwell through a display of her remaining artwork following her murder.
* Oct. 16: The OWU Clay Target team takes first place at the Ohio State Skeet Shoot to open its season.

**November 1991**
* Nov. 19: Delta Tau Delta fraternity receives 50 hours of mandatory community service after being caught with a stolen gravestone.
* Nov. 19: Six OWU students sustain minor injuries after a university van driven by student Naima Johnston crashes at Oak Hill Avenue and Liberty Street.
* Nov. 19: Magic Johnson’s announcement that he contracted HIV prompts widespread discussion on campus regarding health education and AIDS awareness.

**December 1991**
* Dec. 11: President David Warren warns the campus community of an impending fiscal crisis and tighter budget proposals due to the national economic recession and prospective enrollment drops.
* Dec. 11: Two valuable art pieces donated by alumna Barbara Walbridge are stored away from public display due to security concerns over their worth.
* Dec. 11: Senior noseguard Keith Rucker is named to the Kodak All-American football team by the American Football Coaches Association.
* Dec. 11: The OWU Henchmen club hockey team defeats rival Denison 7-2 in a penalty-filled match at the Ohio State Rink.

**January 1992**
* **Jan. 23**: University administrative officials refuse to release campus crime reports, a policy violating new federal regulation interpretations.
* **Jan. 23**: Student radio station WSLN-FM and the journalism department suffer thefts following a break-in at Slocum Hall over winter break.
* **Jan. 23**: Members of the Beta Theta Pi fraternity are charged with possession of firearms and drug paraphernalia following a winter break search.
* **Jan. 23**: Edythe L. "Mom" Betts, housemother for Phi Gamma Delta for 23 years, dies at age 77.
* **Jan. 23**: An editorial announces that the on-campus *Transcript* will cease publication with the edition.

**February 1992**
* **Feb. 11**: Tau Kappa Epsilon president Gillie J. McCreath II and junior Kevin Farrell face disorderly conduct charges from Delaware Police after a bar fight.
* **Feb. 11**: Jean Hopper, coordinator of Academic Advising, announces her retirement after 30 years at OWU.
* **Feb. 11**: Acting Journalism Department Chairman Trace Regan discusses the possibility of making *The Transcript* an independent publication.
* **Feb. 11**: Dean of Student Services Don Chenoweth announces the senior off-campus housing lottery will likely be canceled.
* **Feb. 11**: Faculty prepare to vote on proposed cuts and reforms to the National Colloquium series.
* **Feb. 11**: Five-year development plans are announced to renovate the Memorial Union Building and former OWU Bookstore.
* **Feb. 11**: Blues Traveler is scheduled to perform the spring concert at Branch Rickey Arena on April 16.
* **Feb. 27**: The university reverses a decision to renew the one-year contract of Visiting Assistant Professor Sarah Snyder.
* **Feb. 27**: Safewalk expands its escort services to pick up students at sorority houses.
* **Feb. 27**: Women's basketball clinches its first-ever NCAC championship with a 79-60 victory over Case Western Reserve University.

**March 1992**
* **Mar. 24**: Nineteen-year-old freshman Stephen Westbrook Palmer Jr. dies in Bashford Hall of apparent alcohol poisoning; campus holds memorial services.
* **Mar. 24**: Freshman William MacGillivray is arrested for stealing a fraternity composite photo and assaulting a Public Safety officer.
* **Mar. 24**: Former professor Raymond Paul Leech, 67, dies unexpectedly while exercising on the Selby Stadium track.
* **Mar. 24**: Plans are finalized for the 70-year tradition of the Democratic Mock Convention on April 3–4.
* **Mar. 24**: OWU baseball sweeps Earlham, boosting the team's combined batting average to .353.

**April 1992**
* **Apr. 9**: Athletic department financial issues force drastic reductions in student access to Edwards Gym facilities.
* **Apr. 9**: OWU participates in the regional Ameriflora event, using university funds to plant flowers on campus.
* **Apr. 9**: The Admissions Office targets an incoming fall freshman class of 470 to 490 students.

**May 1992**
* **May 1**: *The Transcript* receives mailings from Holocaust revisionist Gregg Clemmer claiming the Holocaust is a hoax.
* **May 1**: The Wesleyan Council on Student Affairs (WCSA) and faculty members challenge the campus administration ban on distributing condoms.
* **May 1**: Ohio Wesleyan celebrates its 150th anniversary (Sesquicentennial) with the President's Run, a campus picnic, and historical events.
* **May 1**: Senior Keith Rucker signs with the NFL's Phoenix Cardinals following the national draft.
* **May 1**: Board of Trustees approves salary increases of 3.5 percent for administrative and hourly staff, alongside a faculty salary pool increase.
* **May 1**: Counseling Services Director Scott Donaldson is placed on a one-year terminal contract.
* **May 1**: English and Humanities Professor William E. Judd retires after 33 years at the university.
* **May 1**: University President David Warren and administration consider removing the Statement on Student Rights from the course catalog.
* **May 1**: OWU baseball completes a four-game series sweep against NCAC rival Denison.

**January 1993**
- **Jan. 19**: A winter break campus shutdown achieved an estimated $26,500 in energy savings for the university.
- **Jan. 19**: University Provost G. William Benz accepted an appointment as president of Ashland College.
- **Jan. 19**: Freshman Christopher Masters was appointed editor of *The Transcript*.
- **Jan. 19**: Faculty members engaged in debate regarding a proposed multicultural course requirement.
- **Jan. 19**: Sophomore Bo Dobbs of the men's basketball team was named NCAC Player of the Week.

**February 1993**
- **Feb. 16**: Gerald Duff, academic dean at Goucher College, met with campus groups as the second candidate for university provost.
- **Feb. 16**: Christopher Masters resigned from his role as editor of *The Transcript*.
- **Feb. 16**: A Gay/Lesbian/Bisexual Awareness Week poster listing 375 names raised legal concerns regarding potential libel.
- **Feb. 16**: Candidates Sara M. Sheets, Scott F. Gallagher, Mustapha Mohammed, and Tara Hennigan launched campaigns for Graduating Class Trustee.
- **Feb. 16**: Junior Cindy Geiss was named NCAC Women's Track Athlete of the Week.

**March 1993**
- **March 24**: The faculty passed the Non-Euro-American distribution requirement by an 80-20 vote.
- **March 24**: The Gay/Lesbian/Bisexual Alliance organized student participation for the upcoming March on Washington for Lesbian, Gay and Bi-Equal Rights and Liberation.
- **March 24**: Police intercepted Sigma Chi fraternity pledges following a pledge prank.
- **March 24**: Pro-life activists set up 1,100 crosses outside Slocum Hall to symbolize aborted fetuses, sparking debate with pro-choice groups.
- **March 24**: The men's swim team secured its highest finish ever at Nationals, while former professional soccer player Simon Keith visited to speak about competing after a heart transplant.

**April 1993**
- **April 21**: Three Ohio Wesleyan students pleaded not guilty to felonious assault charges involving a fellow student.
- **April 21**: A faculty committee commenced studies on introducing a Japan/East Asian studies program.
- **April 21**: The baseball team swept area rival Otterbein to extend its winning streak to 14 games, while the men's lacrosse team earned a No. 6 national ranking in Division III.

**October 1993**
- **Oct. 6**: Three lacrosse players pleaded guilty to fourth-degree felony aggravated assault following a Jan. 23 attack on a student.
- **Oct. 6**: The Board of Trustees approved guidelines for the Presidential Search Committee, prompting calls from hourly employees for representation on the panel.
- **Oct. 6**: The History Student Advisory Board published a letter alleging a breach of confidentiality within the Faculty Personnel Committee.
- **Oct. 6**: Public Safety reported a decrease in campus alcohol violations compared to the prior year.
- **Oct. 6**: World War II Holocaust documentary *Survivor's Guild* completed filming inside Slocum Hall's journalism offices.
- **Oct. 6**: The football team secured a 27-13 win against Denison, women's cross country won the Earlham Invitational, and men's soccer maintained an undefeated record.

**January 1994**
* **Jan. 19**: The campus mourned the death of freshman football player Trevor Howard Hartley, who died by suicide on Jan. 12.
* **Jan. 19**: Dr. Daniel E. Anderson, a popular philosophy professor, died after a lengthy battle with cancer.
* **Jan. 19**: Presidential Search Committee announced three finalists, with acting Dean Dick Fusch noting a new president was expected by Feb. 5.
* **Jan. 19**: Insufficient pipe insulation caused flooding in the Hamilton-Williams Campus Center on Jan. 10 and 11.
* **Jan. 19**: Rev. Norman Vincent Peale, a 1920 OWU graduate and author of "The Power Of Positive Thinking," died on Dec. 24 in Pawling, N.Y., at age 65.
* **Jan. 19**: T-shirt vendor Joe College, Inc. was removed from the campus center for selling inappropriate T-shirts.
* **Jan. 19**: The campus phonathon reported raising $412,000 toward its $500,000 goal.
* **Jan. 19**: The men's basketball team extended a six-game winning streak with victories over Oberlin and Wooster, while women's basketball built a four-game winning streak.

**March 1994**
* **March 16**: Four OWU students participating in a Habitat for Humanity house-building trip in Louisiana were assaulted by a group of teenagers.
* **March 16**: Information systems updated the university's administrative computer system, altering the student registration process.
* **March 16**: Candidates, including Matt Confer and Jason Moore, formally announced campaigns for WCSA student government positions.
* **March 16**: OWU's grammar hotline gained attention for answering questions from diverse callers, including the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals.
* **March 16**: Spring break athletics featured baseball winning seven of nine games in Florida, men's tennis going 3-2 at Hilton Head, golf taking sixth at the Gordin Classic, and men's lacrosse splitting two games in Maryland.

**September 1994**
* **September 7**: Dr. Thomas B. Courtice officially assumed office as Ohio Wesleyan's 14th president.
* **September 7**: Former U.S. Surgeon General C. Everett Koop opened the university's Colloquium series with a keynote address.
* **September 7**: Campus launched over 60 renovation and construction projects across university facilities.
* **September 7**: OWU secured its sixth consecutive NCAC All-Sports championship title, and nearly two dozen athletes earned All-America honors for the 1993–94 academic year.
* **September 7**: Men's soccer opened the fall season by winning the Fred Myers Invitational for the 11th straight year.

**October 1994**
* **October 26**: Comedian and lecturer Bertice Berry opened OWU's Third Annual Racial Summit in Gray Chapel, addressing racism, sexism, and homophobia.
* **October 26**: Provost William Louthan issued a statement declaring the previous year's Faculty Personnel Committee (FPC) controversy a "dead issue."
* **October 26**: Top-ranked men's soccer remained undefeated with shutouts against Kenyon (5-0) and Denison (2-0).
* **October 26**: Football earned a 40-20 victory over Case Western Reserve at Selby Field after generating over 500 yards of offense.

**January 1995**

* **Jan. 25:** Thomas B. Courtice is named Ohio Wesleyan's 14th president, marked by an inauguration schedule featuring an alumni summit on higher education challenges.
* **Jan. 25:** The campus community feels the impact of a severe earthquake in Kobe, Japan, as both Japanese and American students maintain ties to the region.
* **Jan. 25:** The university library upgrades its facilities by replacing the outdated LS200 system.
* **Jan. 25:** A nearly $1 million renovation project is launched for Roy Rike Field to build a new soccer complex, while the North Coast Athletic Conference (NCAC) conducts a feasibility study on potential expansion by 1997.
* **Jan. 25:** The women's basketball team strengthens its position in second place in the NCAC, while the men's basketball team drops its third consecutive game.

**March 1995**

* **March 22:** A new student-run publication, *Revolving Door*, faces potential legal complications if published unedited, according to faculty advisor Paul Kostyu.
* **March 22:** The National Abortion and Reproductive Rights Action League (NARAL) plans an Activists' Retreat hosted at the Hamilton-Williams Campus Center.
* **March 22:** The state of Ohio issues new driver's licenses designed to be significantly harder for underage students to alter.
* **March 22:** OWU sponsors the first annual Ohio Wesleyan Premiere benefit performance in Gray Chapel to raise funds for battered women's shelters, while the campus prepares to host its annual Little Sibs Weekend.
* **March 22:** In athletics, the men's swimming team finishes 17th at the NCAA Division III championships led by three All-America relay teams, shotputter Sheila Gisbrecht places seventh at the NCAA indoor meet, the men's lacrosse team moves to 4-0 after a spring trip, and the baseball team finishes 7-2 during its Florida trip.

**September 1995**

* **September 6:** Late-summer rainstorms cause roof collapses and structural damage at both Gray Chapel and Elliott Hall two weeks before classes resume.
* **September 6:** Vice President for Business Affairs and Treasurer Louis Szalontai departs his position; meanwhile, OWU enrolls 510 new freshmen out of 2,236 applicants for the Class of 1999, bringing total campus enrollment to approximately 1,650.
* **September 6:** The university launches a new licensing initiative to enter the logo market for added income, while Career Services reports higher employment rates and increased earnings for recent graduates.
* **September 6:** The National Colloquium opens its academic programming around the central theme of the family.
* **September 6:** Margie Shade shifts duties within the athletics department, leaving her position as head women's soccer coach in doubt.

**October 1995**

* **October 25:** U.S. Congresswoman Patricia Schroeder (D-Colo.) addresses campus regarding federal policy on families and children, drawing student protests during her visit.
* **October 25:** Former editor John Ruch ('93) of the independent, off-campus *Transcript* is officially banned from the OWU campus.
* **October 25:** President Courtice appoints a new Task Force on Alcohol Use and Abuse to conduct a campus-wide study on student drinking patterns.
* **October 25:** A $12,000 gift from a university trustee funds the OWU Wind Ensemble's first East Coast tour in six years to assist with student recruitment.
* **October 25:** Public Safety launches a crackdown to curb an increase in campus bicycle thefts.
* **October 25:** In sports, quarterback Dan Hover accounts for three touchdowns as the football team scores 20 fourth-quarter points to defeat Case Reserve 27-7, while the field hockey team contends for its eighth conference title in nine years.

**January 1996**
* **Jan. 24**: The House of Black Culture is invaded and robbed of jewelry, money, and compact disks.
* **Jan. 24**: The OWU community mourns junior Alamgir (Gir) Farhat, who died of severe asthma during winter break.
* **Jan. 24**: Students living on the East Coast face travel delays and stay homebound due to the Blizzard of 1996.
* **Jan. 24**: *The Transcript* introduces a new editor and features photographer Jacob Holdt's documentary work on American lifestyles.
* **Jan. 24**: Greek organizations implement a condensed four-day rush schedule instead of the traditional ten days.
* **Jan. 24**: Men's basketball drops NCAC games to Wittenberg (74-55) and Kenyon; the Lady Bishops drop to 8-7 after a 78-69 loss to Wittenberg.

**March 1996**
* **March 20**: Under a restructuring plan to cut $700,000 from the non-faculty budget, positions held by Dean Don Chenoweth, Associate Dean Bob Brandt, and botany/microbiology instructor Jann Ichida are eliminated.
* **March 20**: Stuyvesant Hall residents face soaring costs due to ongoing community damage charges.
* **March 20**: The Woman's House prepares to host Women's Week from March 23 to March 31.
* **March 20**: Dr. Richard Olson delivers the 1996 Merrick Lectures on Science and Religion.
* **March 20**: The men's baseball team plays in Florida over spring break, while men's lacrosse opens the season 2-1 on their trip.

**September 1996**
* **Sept. 4**: OWU receives a four-year, $650,000 grant from the Howard Hughes Medical Institute for undergraduate biological science programs.
* **Sept. 4**: A generous federal financial aid system boosts enrollment, bringing 705 freshmen to campus.
* **Sept. 4**: Trials begin for six suspects in the Jan. 20 robbery at the House of Black Culture.
* **Sept. 4**: Robert A. Holm becomes executive assistant to the president, and Audry Klimke Carter is hired as a fundraising and management consultant.
* **Sept. 4**: Discussions begin regarding potential renovations for Merrick Hall, which has been condemned for 10 years.
* **Sept. 4**: The university reviews the May 12 commencement, where 361 graduates were awarded degrees.

**October 1996**
* **Oct. 23**: Sophomore Casey Polatsek dies from smoke inhalation following a fire at the Phi Delta Theta fraternity house.
* **Oct. 23**: The WCSA Budgeting Committee considers closing the University Film Series to fund a campus cable movie channel.
* **Oct. 23**: Senior middle linebacker Craig Anderson is named Burger King Scholar Athlete of the Week, bringing national television recognition and a donation to OWU.
* **Oct. 23**: Wittenberg defeats the Battling Bishops 35-12 during FallFest football at Selby Field.
* **Oct. 23**: Recent graduate Obi Moneme ('96) signs a two-year professional contract with the Cleveland Crunch of the National Professional Soccer League.

**January 1997**
- **Jan. 22:** OWU inaugurates an economics exchange program with Germany featuring visiting professor Alexander Karmann.
- **Jan. 22:** A power outage leaves OWU in the dark, affecting 5,901 Delaware residents.
- **Jan. 22:** Residents returning from winter break find a standing pool of water flooding the smaller Creative Arts house.
- **Jan. 22:** Over 100 women participate in campus rush despite cold weather.
- **Jan. 22:** Women's basketball edges Case Western Reserve 64-63 in overtime behind Angie Quatman's 21 points, while men's basketball drops a 71-64 contest to Case Western.
- **Jan. 22:** Coverage reports on a hostage situation involving an OWU student's family following a siege at the Japanese Ambassador's residence in Peru.

**March 1997**
- **Mar. 19:** A committee decision overturning the relocation of the Peace and Justice House to the Creative Arts House site takes effect.
- **Mar. 19:** Following a tuition increase by the Board of Trustees, OWU prepares to hire five new faculty members.
- **Mar. 19:** Fraternities endure vandalism on The Hill, while current residents of the House of Black Culture lose their bid to remain in the house for the upcoming year.
- **Mar. 19:** OWU works to correct an error after discovering international phone calls were overcharged by double over previous months.
- **Mar. 19:** Athletics updates include a $250,000 fundraising push for a new soccer stadium, men's lacrosse defeating Salisbury State, Alison Albrecht finishing 8th in Division III women's track, and swimmer Laura Marean earning honorable mention All-American honors.

**August 1997**
- **Aug. 27:** OWU receives the largest monetary gift in university history—$5.1 million—from late alumni Richard C. and Catherine B. Sharp.
- **Aug. 27:** Total enrollment reaches 1,850 students, including 604 new students (586 freshmen and 18 transfers) representing 35 states and 31 foreign countries.
- **Aug. 27:** OWU President Thomas B. Courtice is named president of the North Coast Athletic Conference (NCAC) for a two-year term.
- **Aug. 27:** OWU advances plans for a virtual community, aiming to allow students to attend classes via computer by spring.
- **Aug. 27:** The theme-based National Colloquium series returns to campus for the fall semester.

**October 1997**
- **Oct. 15:** U.S. Secretary of Defense William S. Cohen accepts an invitation to speak at OWU's 1998 commencement.
- **Oct. 15:** OWU accepts a $2.5 million gift from two Class of 1959 graduates, marking the second-largest living donor gift to the endowment.
- **Oct. 15:** Public Safety reports 14 cases of violence so far in the year, equaling the total reported for all of the previous year and raising student concerns over campus lighting and emergency phones.
- **Oct. 15:** Media critic James Ledbetter and Case Western biology professor Thomas Murray address campus audiences on censorship and public broadcasting.
- **Oct. 15:** Men's basketball coach Gene Mehaffey announces his plan to retire after the 1998-99 season, while football defeats Oberlin College 50-12 behind four touchdowns from freshman Matt Capone.

**January 1998**

* **1998-01-21**: Fraternities faced new occupancy requirements and sororities adopted a "no-frills" format during Rush 1998.
* **1998-01-21**: The Transcript and WCSA co-sponsored an alcohol forum in response to Letters to the Editor regarding alcohol use.
* **1998-01-21**: Delaware Police Captain Mark Drum reported that no arrests had been made in the assault cases from the end of the previous semester, though no related incidents recurred.
* **1998-01-21**: Over 350 Delaware community members, including OWU students and faculty, gathered at an 8 a.m. breakfast to celebrate Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
* **1998-01-21**: Preparations were underway for Mozart's opera *The Magic Flute*, scheduled to open Feb. 26.
* **1998-01-21**: In sports, Camillus scored 31 points to lead the men's basketball team past Case, while freshman Jess Viertlboeck returned from mononucleosis to start for the women's basketball team.

**March 1998**

* **1998-03-18**: WCSA passed a revised alcohol policy outlining minimum sanctions for drug and alcohol offences to present to the faculty.
* **1998-03-18**: DATA planned an experimental weekend shuttle system to take students to High Street near The Ohio State University campus.
* **1998-03-18**: Women's Week, themed "Strength Looks Great on a Woman," began with the attorney from *Roe v. Wade* featured as the keynote speaker.
* **1998-03-18**: The House of Spirituality and PRIDE addressed Public Safety regarding an unresolved incident involving sexual slurs painted over PRIDE symbols.
* **1998-03-18**: Disagreement divided the senior class after a majority voted for residential gym equipment as the senior class gift.
* **1998-03-18**: Professor Richard Spall brought the publication *The Historian* to Ohio Wesleyan, offering student internship opportunities.
* **1998-03-18**: On spring break, the OWU Chamber Singers encountered trouble requiring three different buses across seven states, while the baseball team swept its trip to Florida. Senior Ali Albrecht earned a spot in the shotput at the NCAA Division III track and field nationals.

**May 1998**

* **1998-05-06**: U.S. Secretary of Defense William Cohen was selected to deliver the commencement address, invited by trustee Richard North Patterson ('68).
* **1998-05-06**: Alumni Weekend events were scheduled for May 15–17, featuring the President's Dinner and an open house at Andrews House.
* **1998-05-06**: The Journalism Department recognized its graduating seniors as the Class of 1998 prepared to graduate.

**October 1998**

* **1998-01-14 / 1998-10-14**: Campus security reported a male act of public indecency inside Beeghly Library on Sept. 14.
* **1998-10-14**: Three Power Plant workers faced layoffs due to the installation of a new $4 million gas boiler system.
* **1998-10-14**: Six members of the previous year's baseball team faced upcoming separated trials for misdemeanor assault and disorderly conduct charges.
* **1998-10-14**: The Capital Campaign announced it was $10 million ahead of its fundraising goal.
* **1998-10-14**: National Colloquium presentations featured Professor Akbar Mahdi, Professor Margot Greenlee, and Professor Ted Cohen discussing gender roles and reversals.
* **1998-10-14**: OWU students and local residents participated in the second annual Alternative CropWalk to raise food and funds for those in need, while the seventh annual Pumpkin Run 5K was scheduled to aid Grady Pediatrics.
* **1998-10-14**: In athletics, the Intercollegiate Athletic Commission approved starting a varsity softball team, OWU men's soccer earned the No. 1 spot in the NCAC, and women's soccer defeated Allegheny 3-1.

**January 1999**
* **Jan. 20**: Nearly twelve inches of snow covered campus over winter break, and afternoon classes were canceled following a Level III Snow Emergency.
* **Jan. 20**: Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity was written up by Public Safety on Dec. 10 for possession of illegal alcoholic beverages.
* **Jan. 20**: Exiled Chinese dissident leader Harry Wu was scheduled to speak in Sanborn Hall on human rights in China.
* **Jan. 20**: Rush concluded with 84 women joining sororities and 118 men joining fraternities.
* **Jan. 20**: The women's basketball team secured victories over Case Western and Allegheny, while the injury-plagued men's basketball team suffered two losses.

**March 1999**
* **March 3**: Ohio Wesleyan Chaplain Jon Powers presented a plan to increase campus awareness of the university's United Methodist heritage by 2000.
* **March 3**: WCSA and the administration hosted a forum to discuss converting historic Merrick Hall into student residential apartments.
* **March 3**: A hearing began regarding a racial discrimination lawsuit filed against the university by Kathryn Ogletree.
* **March 3**: D.C. Congresswoman Sabrina Sojourner spoke on diversity and spirituality at a PRIDE event in Gray Chapel.
* **March 3**: The women's basketball team won its first NCAC tournament championship in seven years, defeating Wittenberg 74-72 behind late heroics from Megan Rulon.
* **March 3**: The Office of Admission received $685,000 for new recruitment efforts, while new policies linked financial aid eligibility to drug violation records.

**April 1999**
* **April 21**: Freshman Jude Buwule-Lugudde was arraigned and released on $500 bond after pleading not guilty to rape and sexual battery charges.
* **April 21**: Faculty unanimously voted to block the cancellation of library journals and called proposed amendments to the university harassment policy into review.
* **April 21**: Administrators approved a search committee to find a replacement for departing Director of Student Activities Claudia Spencer.
* **April 21**: Men's lacrosse reached a No. 9 national ranking after a late victory over Denison; baseball swept Wittenberg in a double-header behind Drew Caravella's hitting.
* **April 21**: Black Men of the Future hosted its inaugural BMF Week, and Circle K organized Community Fest on the Welch Hall lawn.

**September 1999**
* **September 15**: President Thomas B. Courtice informed faculty that the university anticipated a $100,000 surplus in unappropriated funds.
* **September 15**: *National Geographic* editor Joel Swerdlow delivered the opening address for the Sagan National Colloquium.
* **September 15**: The Interfraternity Council tabled a proposal to create Greek-only identification cards to restrict party attendance.
* **September 15**: Professors Edward Burtt and Jann Ichida patented a biological solution targeting poultry industry waste issues.
* **September 15**: Football opened the season with a win against Grove City behind a touchdown run by quarterback Phil Heyn.

**October 1999**
* **October 27**: Public Safety and Delaware Police initiated an investigation into an alleged rape reported on campus.
* **October 27**: Renowned Latin American author Carlos Fuentes visited campus as part of the Sagan National Colloquium and Carpenter Lecture series.
* **October 27**: Perkins Observatory welcomed back its main mirror after a 40-year absence.
* **October 27**: University officials presented a proposal to move the Student Health Center into Stuyvesant Hall.
* **October 27**: The defending national champion men's soccer team fell out of the national Top 25 rankings after holding the No. 1 spot earlier in the season.

**January 2000**
- Jan. 26: President Thomas Courtice presents the administration's 2000–2001 proposed budget to WCSA prior to the Board of Trustees vote.
- Jan. 26: Fraternities adjust to a new Greek recruitment plan that results in fewer bids compared to previous rush weeks.
- Jan. 26: A fatal van crash involving a Kenyon College swimmer prompts OWU to examine the safety of its student-driven university vans.
- Jan. 26: Four OWU student-athletes from football and women's soccer earn All-America honors following successful fall seasons.

**February 2000**
- Feb. 2: The Board of Trustees approves the university budget and calls for increased investment in Information Systems.
- Feb. 2: Plans are announced to relocate the Health Center and Student Fitness Center into the Stuyvesant Cafeteria.
- Feb. 9: OWU hosts its traditional Mock Convention in Gray Chapel featuring guest political speakers.
- Feb. 23: Senior Nicole Dailey wins election as Class Trustee in the first single-ballot victory since 1994.
- Feb. 23: Women's basketball clinches the NCAC championship title before advancing to the conference tournament.

**March 2000**
- March 1: David Cozzens resigns as chair of student life, effective June 30.
- March 1: Campus community mourns former OWU student Conor O'Brien, who died by suicide on Feb. 26.
- March 22: Senior Jeremy Granick dies in a single-vehicle automobile accident over spring break.
- March 22: Registrar Mary Jean Roach announces her retirement after 35 years at OWU, including 28 as registrar.
- March 29: OWU faculty votes 81-3 to approve a revised university sexual harassment policy.

**April 2000**
- April 5: Zach Dunlap and Nicole Kirkwood win the WCSA presidential and vice-presidential election by 257 votes.
- April 5: Inter-Fraternity Council leaders encourage fraternity members not to sign proposed housing contracts.
- April 19: Due to pending NCAA legislation, the OWU equestrian team must transition from club to varsity status.
- April 26: Phi Gamma Delta (Fiji) announces it will become a substance-free house beginning in August.
- April 26: Men's track team makes history as the first NCAC squad to win the All-Ohio Invitational championship.

**September 2000**
- Sept. 6: Housing shortages force Residential Life to give 34 seniors late permission to move off-campus shortly before classes start.
- Sept. 6: Public Safety Director Fred Moyer resigns over the summer; John M. Delaney assumes the role of Dean of Students.
- Sept. 13: The Academic Resource Center (ARC) opens in the R.W. Corns Building, merging academic skills, writing, and support services.
- Sept. 20: Voter turnout drops to 17.12% during the WCSA Geographical Representative elections.

**October 2000**
- Oct. 4: OWU receives a $1.2 million gift for science departments from the estate of alumnus David Smith ('53).
- Oct. 4: Women's House sponsors a candlelight vigil following a series of nighttime assaults reported on and near campus.
- Oct. 11: Board of Trustees allocates $625,000 to President Courtice during their first annual full meeting.
- Oct. 25: Buildings and Grounds initiates renovations to convert Humphreys Art Hall into the Richard M. Ross Museum.

**November 2000**
- Nov. 1: Robin Olson is named the new director of Public Safety.
- Nov. 8: Men's soccer defeats Denison 3-0 to secure its third consecutive NCAC championship and an NCAA playoff berth.
- Nov. 8: National coverage highlights Texas Gov. George W. Bush securing Florida's 25 electoral votes in the presidential race against Al Gore.
- Nov. 29: Men's soccer finishes its season following a loss in the NCAA Division III quarterfinal round.

**December 2000**
- Dec. 6: WCSA votes to allocate $5,000 to student radio station WSLN for equipment upgrades and $5,000 to Habitat for Humanity.
- Dec. 6: Women's basketball opens NCAC play with a 76-61 victory over Wooster, led by Katy Sturtz's 29 points.

**January 2001**
* **Jan. 24:** Resident Assistants (RAs) and Small Living Unit (SLU) moderators receive a $500 raise for the 2001-2002 academic year, marking the first pay increase since 1997.
* **Jan. 24:** Twenty-two OWU students travel to Washington, D.C., to participate in protests during the presidential inauguration.
* **Jan. 24:** OWU alumna Erum Ahmed is charged with using the Internet to stalk professor Conrad A. Kent, with whom she previously had a sexual affair.
* **Jan. 24:** The OWU Board of Trustees schedules its annual winter meeting on campus ahead of the Graduating Class Trustee elections.
* **Jan. 24:** WCSA allocates $4,373 in funding to support the campus club ice hockey team.
* **Jan. 24:** Alpha Sigma Phi fraternity members step in to run operations at the Strand Theatre for a charity event.

**March 2001**
* **March 7:** Junior Patrick Riepenhoff wins the Graduating Class Trustee runoff election against Zach Dunlap.
* **March 7:** Three banners (Black History Month, Rafiki Wa Afrika, and Pride) are stolen from the Atrium in a reported hate crime.
* **March 7:** Actress and alumna Wendie Malick is announced as the commencement speaker for the May 13, 2001 ceremony.
* **March 7:** *The Transcript* announces a shift to a bi-weekly publication schedule due to financial concerns.
* **March 7:** The Wellness Center begins offering Lunelle, a monthly injectable birth control option, for $22.
* **March 7:** The men's lacrosse team defeats the Columbus Club Landsharks 17-8 on Feb. 25.

**September 2001**
* **Sept. 5:** Construction begins on the new OWU Science Center, while art classes move into the newly renovated Edgar Hall.
* **Sept. 5:** The national office of Beta Theta Pi disbands OWU's oldest fraternity chapter following a three-year review.
* **Sept. 5:** Provost William Louthan issues a written reprimand to Professor Conrad Kent regarding his relationship with alumna Erum Ahmed.
* **Sept. 5:** Alpha Sigma Phi returns to "The Hill" after moving into a new fraternity house.
* **Sept. 5:** The Sircam computer virus infects hundreds of computers across the campus network.
* **Sept. 5:** Women's soccer opens the season with a 4-0 win over John Carroll and a 2-1 loss to Nazareth College.

**October 2001**
* **Oct. 10:** Former OWU student Matthew Ault is arrested on Oct. 2 for forgery, identity theft, and grand theft after using another student's ID card to secure a loan.
* **Oct. 10:** Author Richard North Patterson ('68) addresses students and faculty at Gray Chapel during a PALS event.
* **Oct. 10:** Thirteen OWU students camp outdoors with Habitat for Humanity to simulate homelessness and raise awareness.
* **Oct. 10:** OWU hosts the All-Ohio Cross Country meet for the 28th time.
* **Oct. 10:** The football team improves to 5-0 on the season following a 45-10 victory against Earlham.

**November 2001**
* **Nov. 7:** OWU approves $10,000 to install an additional T1 line to relieve campus Internet congestion.
* **Nov. 7:** The university distributes a campus-wide survey to gauge student feedback on potentially restricting or banning smoking on campus.
* **Nov. 7:** Laurie Garrett delivers a campus lecture addressing national public health concerns.
* **Nov. 7:** Senior Chris Kittredge wins Kappa Alpha Theta's second annual "Mr. OWU" philanthropy contest.
* **Nov. 7:** Women's soccer captures its fourth consecutive NCAC championship with a 2-0 defeat of Kenyon.
* **Nov. 7:** Football defeats Oberlin 48-13 in conference play.

**January 2002**
* **Jan. 23:** Poet b.f. maiz addresses students in the Benes Room on the legacy of Martin Luther King Jr. during a tribute celebration.
* **Jan. 23:** The Campus Council/WCSA supports socially responsible investing and prepares budget proposals for the Board of Trustees.
* **Jan. 23:** OWU professor and swim coach Richard Hawes carries the Olympic torch en route to Salt Lake City.
* **Jan. 23:** Formal sorority recruitment draws 80 new women into campus chapters.
* **Jan. 23:** Women's basketball defeats Earlham College 83-72 without leading scorer Katie Sturtz, while men's basketball defeats Allegheny 70-63.

**February 2002**
* **Feb. 27:** Greg Moore ('76) and Nina Henderson Moore are named commencement speakers, and Beth Ardale is elected Graduating Class Trustee.
* **Feb. 27:** A formal written fraternization policy is presented to faculty, and Kappa Sigma fraternity prepares to return to campus after a 19-year absence.
* **Feb. 27:** Writer Kevin Powell speaks to students on Black History Month, while students observe Rice Bowl Day in the Atrium to learn about world hunger.
* **Feb. 27:** Women's basketball defeats top-seeded Wittenberg 81-75 in overtime to win the NCAC tournament title.
* **Feb. 27:** Men's lacrosse captures a comeback victory against Lynchburg at Selby Field.

**April 2002**
* **April 10:** WCSA passes election guidelines transitioning all student government voting to an online system starting in the fall.
* **April 10:** Journalist Coleman McCarthy speaks on social injustice during Peace & Justice Week.
* **April 10:** OWU hosts 169 prospective students for "Slice of College Life" alongside the annual Monnett/Kids and Sibs weekend.
* **April 10:** Junior Emily Thornton throws the first no-hitter in OWU softball history.

**September 2002**
* **Sept. 25:** WCSA announces results for geographical representative elections, and the National Colloquium hosts "The Idea of An American Century."
* **Sept. 25:** The Carolyn Dorfman Dance Company performs at the Chappelear Drama Center.
* **Sept. 25:** Renovation continues at the former Delaware Post Office building to house the Richard M. Ross Art Museum and art department classrooms.
* **Sept. 25:** Field hockey drops a close match to Kenyon College by a score of 1-0.

**October 2002**
* **Oct. 30:** The campus community mourns student Jennifer Lynn Dixon, who passed away following an automobile accident.
* **Oct. 30:** The Richard M. Ross Art Museum officially opens its "A Thousand Hounds" exhibition, and Midnight Monorail performs at the Red and Black Review during Homecoming.
* **Oct. 30:** Reports highlight financial stress as OWU draws from its endowment fund, while water leak damage is reported at the campus dance studio.
* **Oct. 30:** Football falls 58-17 to Wabash on Homecoming, while men's soccer earns a 4-0 shutout against Earlham.

**January 2003**
* **Jan. 29:** New federal regulations regarding the SEVIS database complicate administration for OWU's approximately 200 international students.
* **Jan. 29:** The Student Government (WCSA) confronts InfoSys in a roundtable discussion regarding $48,000 allocated for campus Internet bandwidth improvements.
* **Jan. 29:** The OWU theatre department stages James Valcq’s 1950s sci-fi musical *Zombies from the Beyond* in the studio theatre.
* **Jan. 29:** Men's basketball star Travis Schwab is featured as one of OWU’s top varsity athletes.
* **Jan. 29:** International coverage reports UN inspectors requesting more time in Iraq, North Korea rejecting UN nuclear agency authority, shelling along the Kashmir border, and 40 fatalities in an Indian bus-truck collision.

**February 2003**
* **Feb. 26:** Political experts and scholars gather at OWU for a panel discussing "What Will Be Left Of The Bush Agenda?"
* **Feb. 26:** The Chaplain's Office and Career Services receive a $2 million Lilly Endowment grant to support university programming.
* **Feb. 26:** The OWU Bridge Club qualifies for national team championships after defeating Harvard and Columbia.
* **Feb. 26:** Gray Chapel hosts Eve Ensler's *The Vagina Monologues* as part of the V-Day College Campaign.
* **Feb. 26:** Rafiki wa Afrika hosts the annual African Fest for Black History Month, while Tauheed hosts an Eid dinner attended by over 300 people.
* **Feb. 26:** Alleyn Harned is elected senior class trustee; Career Services takes over coordination of Student Assistantship Positions (StAP).
* **Feb. 26:** Global news highlights France and Germany proposing an alternative Iraq disarmament plan, while Saddam Hussein challenges President Bush to a televised debate.

**April 2003**
* **Apr. 9:** Ten OWU Model Arab League students and advisor Akbar Mahdi attend the national conference in Washington, D.C.
* **Apr. 9:** Amnesty International presents a dramatic reading in HWCC Atrium for AIDS Action Week.
* **Apr. 9:** Counting Crows are slated to perform at Spring Fest 2003 during their world tour.
* **Apr. 9:** OWU men's lacrosse defeats Kenyon 16-13 at Selby Stadium, while student Noah Jay-Bonn finishes fourth in the Intermediate Footbag Championships.
* **Apr. 9:** International reports cover U.S. forces seizing Saddam Hussein's palace in Baghdad, prison sentences for Cuban dissidents, and severe casualties reported in Congo's civil war.

**September 2003**
* **Sep. 17:** OWU welcomes 599 incoming students in the Class of 2007, marking an increase in enrollment, academic profile, and diversity.
* **Sep. 17:** University officials announce a task force to revise OWU’s decade-old affirmative action hiring policy for faculty and staff.
* **Sep. 17:** The Sagan National Colloquium on world hunger opens with lectures by author Frances Moore Lappé, Dr. Karyl Thomas Rattay, and Dr. Donald Winkelmann.
* **Sep. 17:** Women's soccer earns its 51st consecutive victory by beating 14th-ranked DePauw 3-0, while varsity football falls 21-0 to Olivet in the season opener.
* **Sep. 17:** Plans are finalized for the Oct. 3 dedication of the Richard M. Ross Art Museum.

**October 2003**
* **Oct. 22:** Late alumna Marian Rudd ('28) bestows a $4.4 million estate gift to Ohio Wesleyan.
* **Oct. 22:** President Thomas B. Courtice approves replacing 10 faculty positions for 2004-2005 but denies requests to add new faculty positions.
* **Oct. 22:** Beeghly Library announces plans to eliminate unlimited free printing in the computer lab starting the following semester.
* **Oct. 22:** WCSA passes a motion to ban resident assistants from serving on the campus Judicial Board in future terms.
* **Oct. 22:** Central Ohio Symphony Orchestra opens its 25th anniversary season at Gray Chapel, while OWU ice hockey opens its season with a 3-0 win over Wittenberg.

**January 2004**
* **Jan. 28:** President Thomas Courtice announces his retirement after 10 years of service.
* **Jan. 28:** The Board of Trustees approves the 2004-05 budget and a $22 million campaign to renovate and expand athletic and recreational facilities.
* **Jan. 28:** Printing restrictions and per-page charges take effect at Beeghly Library.
* **Jan. 28:** Senior Nadir Pracha returns to campus after being denied U.S. re-entry due to NSEERS registration issues.
* **Jan. 28:** Plans are finalized for the 22nd quadriennial Mock Convention, and the Campus Programming Board books The Roots and Blackalicious to headline Springfest.
* **Jan. 28:** Buns Restaurant re-opens in downtown Delaware following a devastating 2002 fire.
* **Jan. 28:** In sports, men's basketball rebounds from a loss to Wittenberg by beating Earlham, while women's basketball posts a 6-2 record in pursuit of the NCAC title.

**March 2004**
* **Mar. 3:** Residential Life announces the "Senior Year Experience" program for Smith Hall East and approves a male student to live in the Women's House.
* **Mar. 3:** Over 300 students and faculty attend a premiere screening of *The Passion of the Christ*, while WCSA moves to amend the campus drinking games policy.
* **Mar. 3:** Student groups engage in service, with 29 Habitat for Humanity volunteers traveling to Miami for spring break construction projects.
* **Mar. 3:** The university hosts African Festival 2004 in the Benes Rooms and a guest lecture on "Radical Honesty" by psychologist Brad Blanton.
* **Mar. 3:** In athletics, men's basketball finishes its most successful season in 16 years after a tournament loss, marking the end of standout Travis Schwab's career. Men's lacrosse opens its season with a 14-1 victory over fifth-ranked Lynchburg.

**April 2004**
* **Apr. 14:** Sections of the floor in Stuyvesant Hall's Smoker are declared structurally unsafe, forcing closures.
* **Apr. 14:** Beeghly Library tests campus wireless internet access, and the newly established Residence Hall Association (RHA) holds its first meeting.
* **Apr. 14:** Public Safety Officer John Ciochetty prepares a book documenting OWU ghost lore, while the Zoology Museum completes its relocation to the Conrades-Wetherell Science Center.
* **Apr. 14:** Over 150 student volunteers sign up to support Springfest as Kappa Sigma fraternity begins efforts to charter on campus after a 22-year absence.
* **Apr. 14:** In athletics, men's lacrosse completes a season sweep of rival Denison, golf wins the Ted Barclay Invitational, and second baseman Linsey Longstreth leads softball to a 12-8 start.

**September 2004**
* **Sep. 22:** Ohio Wesleyan rises to 92nd in *U.S. News & World Report's* top 100 national liberal arts colleges.
* **Sep. 22:** Audry Carter steps down as Vice President for University Relations, Edward Kahn takes over as chair of Theatre and Dance, and head baseball coach Roger Ingles is named interim Director of Athletics.
* **Sep. 22:** Alpha Sigma Phi receives the Grand Senior President's award for top national chapter, while Suparna Bhaskaran assumes leadership of the Women's and Gender Studies program.
* **Sep. 22:** Student Life sees the launch of OWU's first all-female a cappella group and the C.L.E.A.R. initiative promoting alcohol-free activities.
* **Sep. 22:** In athletics, women's rugby opens with a 32-0 shutout of Ohio Northern, women's tennis sweeps all flights at the Kenyon Invitational, and both soccer teams earn national Division III top-20 rankings.

**October 2004**
* **Oct. 27:** Activist Gloria Steinem speaks at a campus lunch, comedian Bill Cosby performs two shows at Gordon Field House, and MTV’s *Rock the Vote* tour stops on campus.
* **Oct. 27:** Gray Chapel hosts a broadcast town-hall debate ahead of the presidential election, complementing five OWU students interning in Washington, D.C.
* **Oct. 27:** The Strand Theatre seeks state funding to study converting the venue into a university and community performing arts center.
* **Oct. 27:** Chi Phi hosts its 20th annual charity haunted house, and the Astronomy Club holds a public viewing for a lunar eclipse.
* **Oct. 27:** In sports, football defeats Kenyon 30-24 for its third consecutive win during Homecoming, while men's soccer defeats Kenyon and Denison to stay near the top of the NCAC.

**January 2005**
- **Jan. 26:** The Board of Trustees approves a 4.9 percent tuition, room, and board increase for the 2005-06 academic year.
- **Jan. 26:** Campus groups form the "Against the Tide" task force to organize fundraising for Asian tsunami relief.
- **Jan. 26:** WCSA forms a cultural sensitivity task force following concerns that a fight outside the House of Black Culture was racially motivated.
- **Jan. 26:** Disqualifications in WCSA elections leave Bashford Hall and Smith West without Geographical Representatives, forcing a revote.
- **Jan. 26:** The House of H.O.P.E. announces it will not reapply for SLU status for 2005-06, prompting a proposal from the Athenaeum to fill the vacancy.
- **Jan. 26:** Senior Heather Costello earns a American Society for Microbiology fellowship.
- **Jan. 26:** The Student Activities Office and CPB announce Guster will headline Springfest in April.
- **Jan. 26:** Lady Bishops basketball beats Oberlin 91-63 led by Erica Brizendine and Kelly Heil, while men's basketball falls to Wittenberg 61-49.

**March 2005**
- **March 3:** The SLU Review Committee approves Habitat for Humanity House to fill the SLU spot left vacant by the disbanding House of H.O.P.E.
- **March 3:** Over 100 students prepare to embark on 10 Spring Break mission trips following a send-off prayer service led by Chaplain Jon Powers.
- **March 3:** Central Ohio Symphony Orchestra welcomes President Mark Huddleston with a Gray Chapel concert.
- **March 3:** WCSA works to restructure and clarify OWU's campus alcohol policy.
- **March 3:** The OWU Investment Club places third in a national year-long investing competition among 20 schools for the second consecutive year.
- **March 3:** Men's club hockey finishes third in the inaugural Bishop Invitational, while women's basketball ends its season 17-10 after a 53-42 loss to Kenyon in the NCAC semifinals.

**April 2005**
- **April 14:** Trustees approve President Huddleston’s 2005-06 budget and a three-year plan to erase a $2 million deficit.
- **April 14:** Faculty consider an Academic Policies Committee proposal to add a quantitative ("Q") course graduation requirement.
- **April 14:** An anonymous $1.5 million pledge is announced for the "Remembering Mr. Rickey" campaign for a new natatorium and turf facility.
- **April 14:** City and university officials discuss adding lighting to the South Liberty Street and Rowland Avenue crosswalk following a December accident involving three students.
- **April 14:** Guster performs at Springfest, kicking off their tour at OWU.
- **April 14:** Kappa Alpha Theta wins Sigma Chi's Derby Days for the second straight year.
- **April 14:** OWU Baseball sweeps a four-game series against Wabash, and third baseman Sammy Hall is named NCAC Player of the Week.

**September 2005**
- **Sept. 29:** Homecoming weekend features benefit concerts, the Red and Black Revue, and the induction of nine former athletes into the OWU Athletic Hall of Fame.
- **Sept. 29:** OWU launches a nationwide search for a new provost and a new director of Public Safety.
- **Sept. 29:** Professor Emeritus of Botany-Microbiology Dr. Allan Ai Ichida dies at age 76.
- **Sept. 29:** 80-year-old Jacob Rupple enrolls as a sophomore at OWU.
- **Sept. 29:** Religion professor Emmanuel Twesigye speaks on race, age, and class in relation to Hurricane Katrina's impact on the Gulf region.
- **Sept. 29:** Former GEICO executive Louis A. Simpson (’58) delivers a lecture on shareholder value.
- **Sept. 29:** Coaches begin joining Public Safety officers on evening campus patrols.

**November 2005**
- **Nov. 3:** Gray Chapel hosts musical comedian Stephen Lynch for a headlining performance.
- **Nov. 3:** Student departmental boards begin evaluating 95 faculty members for tenure, promotion, and retention.
- **Nov. 3:** OWU hosts an Earthquake Relief Buffet for Southern Asia and a Cultural Food Festival in the Benes Rooms.
- **Nov. 3:** Beeghly Library marks 160 years as a federal government document depository.
- **Nov. 3:** The #2 ranked men's soccer team defeats Wittenberg 3-0 to advance to the NCAC tournament final with a 19-0 record, while women's soccer defeats Kenyon 3-2 to advance to their final.

**February 2006**
* **Feb. 1**: The Board of Trustees approves a 7 percent tuition hike for the upcoming year and agrees to increase the student activity fee.
* **Feb. 1**: Vice President of University Relations Mark Richter resigns after serving for approximately one year.
* **Feb. 1**: The Minority Student Affairs budget receives a $10,000 increase for the 2006-2007 fiscal year, while the Annual Giving Fund raises its target to $3.6 million.
* **Feb. 1**: The OWU men's basketball team sets a Branch Rickey Arena record with 16 three-pointers during a 121-70 victory over Hiram.
* **Feb. 16**: Emmy Award-winning CBS correspondent Byron Pitts ('82) is named commencement speaker for the May 14 graduation ceremony.
* **Feb. 16**: Campus Chaplain John Powers and campus forums address international tensions following the publication of anti-Muslim cartoons in the Middle East.
* **Feb. 16**: Men's basketball players Andy Warnock and Ben Chojnacki earn ESPN The Magazine Academic All-District IV honors.

**March 2006**
* **March 9**: Mark Hubbart Shipps ('70) is named Vice President of University Relations, effective July 1, 2006.
* **March 9**: The Academic Policy Committee proposes modifying the Group II Natural Sciences distribution requirement to include mathematics courses.
* **March 9**: "How Science Influences Who We Are" is announced as the 2006 Sagan National Colloquium theme.
* **March 9**: A temporary boil order is placed on University, Slocum, and Sturges halls due to water safety concerns.
* **March 30**: Juniors Marie Rymut and Dale Stewart are elected WCSA president and vice president, defeating Ben Owen and Bob Matthews.
* **March 30**: OWU begins its search for a new Public Safety director, scheduling candidate interviews.
* **March 30**: Sammy Hall hits three home runs and drives in 12 RBIs to lead the baseball team in a four-game sweep over Earlham at Littick Field.

**April 2006**
* **April 20**: Faculty members approve six revisions to the university's official Alcohol Policy.
* **April 20**: WCSA allocates $220,043 to campus organizations for the upcoming academic year, representing a nearly $40,000 increase over the previous year.
* **April 20**: Plans are announced for exterior renovations to historic Merrick Hall, which has remained vacant since the 1980s.
* **April 20**: A *Transcript* survey reveals that OWU students contribute approximately $842,400 annually to the local downtown Delaware economy.
* **April 20**: The second annual OWU Documentary Film Festival takes place at The Strand Theatre, showcasing student honors projects.
* **April 20**: Men's lacrosse scores 11 unanswered goals to defeat Wittenberg 13-6 at Selby Stadium.
